Terms & Definitions

1332-term reference dictionary of economics, finance and stock market terminology; definitions compiled from official sources such as TCMB, Competition Authority, Development Agencies and economics dictionaries. For basic concepts, Stock Market Glossary' what, for accounting terminology Accounting Terms you can check the page.

A

Abuse of Dominant Position

Undertakings holding significant market power can influence competitive conditions in the market more easily than their rivals. The abuse by dominant undertakings of this power in ways that restrict competition in the market is prohibited under Article 6 of the Competition Act (Law No. 4054). What matters in assessments under Article 6 is that a dominant position itself is not prohibited. An undertaking's market power may result from technological superiority, efficiency or a quality product/service.

fair income distribution fair income distribution

The state in which the inhabitants of a country have equal opportunity in production and consumption and receive the share they deserve.

fair insurance policy fairly priced insurance policy

An insurance policy whose premium is set to equal the expected value of that policy.

Administered Price

Prices set by undertakings or by the state that do not change in the face of short-term fluctuations in supply and demand conditions. According to some economists, this price rigidity stems from market power.

moral hazard moral hazard

The phenomenon of economic units making riskier choices when the cost of an adverse outcome will be paid by others.

Letter of Credit Letter of Credit

A type of guarantee concerning the payment for exported goods, under which payment will be made once certain conditions are fulfilled. Banks or other financial institutions intermediate letter-of-credit transactions. Accordingly, a letter of credit is a kind of letter of guarantee sent by a financial institution to a correspondent bank in a foreign country, committing it to extend credit on its own account for a certain period, in a certain amount and in favor of a third party.

active job search active job search

; activities such as applying to a job-finding institution or directly to an employer, searching for a job via the Internet or newspapers, taking oral or written job exams or interviews, preparing to start one's own business.

rational expectations hypothesis rational expectations hypothesis

The view that economic units take into account all past and forward-looking information when making forecasts about the future.

liquidity liquidity

A conceptual measure describing how easily and quickly a financial asset can be converted into equivalent cash.

Algorithmic Collusion

An algorithm is expressed as a path designed to reach a goal, a set of steps followed; in computer science it is defined as the method by which software performs a task. Algorithms can, for example, be used by undertakings as a price-setting tool in online shopping. An undertaking can monitor a rival's product prices through algorithms and set its own prices accordingly. At a more advanced level, algorithms cease to be a tool of competition

Allocation of Common Costs

The allocation by a multi-product undertaking of its general expenses separately to the production costs of these products. While distributing general expenses among its products, the undertaking may take into account the demand elasticity of those products or the competitive constraints in the markets where they operate. For example, it may exclude general expenses from a product operating in a competitive market with high demand elasticity while keeping its price low in that market.

Buying Delegation

A delegation of representatives of institutions and organizations, media members, producers and importers brought to the country to purchase goods or services, coordinated by the Ministry of Trade in cooperation with exporters' associations and/or organizing bodies, with the aim of increasing exports.

Call Option Call Option

It gives the option holder the right to buy the good, asset or financial indicator underlying the option at the price written in the contract at the contract's maturity, without incurring any obligation.

Written call options are treated as liabilities.( Written call options are treated as liabilities.

English definition: Contracts giving the right to buy an asset.

Bid Bid

The price at which market participants are willing to buy assets traded in the market (such as foreign currency or securities).

Bid-Ask Spread Bid-Ask Spread

Expresses the difference between the bid and ask prices of any traded security.

A narrow bid-ask spread indicates a liquid market.( A narrow bid-ask spread indicates a liquid market.

English definition: The difference between the best bid and best ask price.

goal independence goal independence

The central bank's setting of its own monetary policy targets.

Amnesty Plus

Under the additional leniency rule, those who cannot benefit from the leniency program in an investigation concerning one market may, if they apply with respect to a cartel in another market, benefit from immunity for the second cartel and receive a reduction in the fines arising from the first cartel. In Turkish competition law, the provision on this subject is made in Article 7(2) of the Fining Regulation.

Ana faiz oranı prime interest rate

The rate that forms the basis of the interest banks charge for credit.

Analitik Bilanço/TCMB Analitik Bilançosu Analytical Balance Sheet/CBRT Analytical Balance Sheet

An analytical balance sheet is one in which the accounts on the asset and liability sides are netted against one another and consolidated under appropriate groupings. The CBRT Analytical Balance Sheet consolidates the items on the CBRT balance sheet taking into account the items relevant to the effective conduct of monetary policy, without detailed breakdowns. In line with the functioning of monetary policy, 'Foreign Assets', 'Domestic Assets' and 'Valuation Account' appear under 'Assets', while 'Total Foreign Currency Liabilities' and 'Central Bank Money' appear under 'Liabilities'. For the CBRT Analytical Balance Sheet

Anti-Competitive Agreements

Refers to the secret or open agreements of a restrictive nature on competition made among undertakings. Such agreements can be horizontal or vertical in nature.

Ara hedef intermediate target

A target that can directly influence the main target of monetary policy and is more transparent and measurable than the main target.

Ara mal intermediate good

Products that are used up in the production process or become part of a final good.

Aracı Kurum

Joint-stock companies authorized by the Capital Markets Board to engage in capital market activities.

Example: An investment entity does not consolidate its controlled investees but measures them at fair value.( An investment entity does not consolidate its controlled investees but measures them at fair value.

English definition: An entity that obtains funds from investors to provide them with investment management services and measures its investments at fair value through profit or loss.

Arakazanç Ticareti Carry Trade

Borrowing in a lower-interest (lower-cost) currency and deploying the loan by investing in a higher-interest (higher-yield) currency. The net return of the carry trade is determined by exchange rate developments, under the assumption that credit risk remains constant.

Aralık içinde dalgalanma floating within a band

An exchange rate regime in which nominal exchange rates are allowed to move within a certain band around a central parity set by the central bank.

Araç bağımsızlığı instrument independence

The central bank's setting of its own policy instruments to achieve its targets.

Arbitraj Arbitrage

The transaction of making a profit by simultaneously buying a security, currency or commodity in one market and selling it in another (exchanging the securities with one another). Arbitrage transactions lead to a reduction in price differences between markets. Today, with the growth of communication technology and the falling cost of accessing information, price differences between markets are extremely low, and any differences that appear are instantly eliminated by such transactions.

Artan fiyat ihalesi ascending price auction

Or the English auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively raised, starting from a low price, until the winner is determined.

Artan gider endüstrisi increasing cost industry

An industry in which firms' average total costs rise as the market grows.

Artan oranlı vergilendirme progressive taxation

A taxation system in which the tax rate rises as the amount subject to tax increases.

Arz supply

A fundamental economic concept describing how much of a product sellers in the market want to sell, and can sell, in a given period.

Arz esnekliği elasticity of supply

Or the price elasticity of supply, in short εS: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity supplied of a product changes as a result of a one percent increase in its price.

Arz eğrisi supply curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity supplied, all else being constant.

Arz fazlası excess supply

Or surplus: the situation in which the quantity supplied in the market exceeds the quantity demanded.

Arz çizelgesi supply schedule

A list showing how much of a product is supplied at different price levels in a given period.

Arz şoku supply shock

A change in aggregate supply in the economy due to an effect other than the general price level.

Arzın fiyat esnekliği price elasticity of supply

Or supply elasticity, in short εS: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity supplied of a product changes as a result of a one percent increase in its price.

Asgari geçim indirimi minimum living allowance

The exemption of a certain portion of wages from tax.

Asgari ücret minimum wage

The lowest wage set by the state as the compensation of labor for a certain period, which cannot be reduced by mutual agreement.

Asil-vekil sorunu principal-agent problem

When the authority to carry out a transaction is delegated by the principal to the agent, the agent's acting in line with its own interests due to asymmetric information.

Asimetrik bilgi asymmetric information

The situation in which one of the parties to an economic activity has more information than the other.

Asit-test oranı Quick ratio / Acid-test ratio

A liquidity ratio calculated from the current ratio by excluding inventories ((Current Assets − Inventories) / Short-Term Liabilities); it measures the most liquid items.

Association of Undertakings

Undertaking associations can from time to time direct their members through recommendation decisions in line with their founding purposes. Such recommendations may relate to sales prices and similar matters and may carry purposes and/or effects that restrict competition. It must be determined whether the recommendations of undertaking associations result directly in binding decisions of the association. Indeed, binding undertaking association decisions restrict competition

Assured Base of Sales

The core sales of undertakings refer to the sales they can make without feeling the competitive pressure of their rivals, as a result of factors such as brand image, product/service quality, accessibility and after-sales service quality. An undertaking having core sales means that a certain (inelastic) part of total demand in the market depends on that undertaking. Undertakings with market power are generally accepted to have core sales

Atık Bertaraf

The orderly and continuous storage of solid, liquid and gaseous wastes, their elimination by burning, and their conversion into products and energy for recovery. Preliminary Project: a draft prepared before the implementation project that gives an idea about the main project.

Avans Advance Payment

The transaction of lending against commercial bills and documents taken as collateral, as well as government bonds and exchange-listed bonds.

Example: The customer paid an advance of 10.000 before the equipment was delivered.( The customer paid a 10.000 advance before delivery of the equipment.

English definition: A payment made by a customer before goods or services are delivered, creating an obligation on the seller.

Average Total Cost

The costs obtained by dividing total costs, including variable and fixed costs, by the total quantity produced.

in-kind income in-kind income

Non-monetary earnings provided to households in the form of goods and services by the state or employers.

In-kind Contribution

A contribution made in a project by the project owner and/or its partners in the form of land, goods, materials, labor, machinery and equipment to meet the project's specific needs. B2B: an abbreviation of Business to Business, this term refers to any commercial activity that businesses carry out directly with one another. B2C: an abbreviation of Business to Consumer, this term refers to any commercial activity that businesses carry out directly with consumers

goods competing for the same resource goods competing for the same resource

Products obtained from a common resource that can be used a limited number of times.

Disaggregation STRIP - Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal of Securities

Refers to the stripping of a coupon-bearing security so that its principal and coupons can be traded separately. The aim is, in particular, to broaden the scope of use of long-term coupon-bearing issues from the investor's perspective and to increase demand for such issues. For this purpose, the Undersecretariat of Treasury can strip the Government Domestic Debt Securities it has auctioned and the Lease Certificates it has sold directly into their principals and coupons.

Bear Market Bear Market

Refers to markets in which prices are falling.

descending price auction descending price auction

Or the Dutch auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively lowered, starting from a high price, until a buyer emerges.

law of diminishing returns law of diminishing returns

A fundamental economic concept stating that while at least one production factor is fixed, the contribution to production of an increase in another variable factor will gradually diminish.

decreasing cost industry decreasing cost industry

An industry in which firms' average total costs fall as the market grows.

law of diminishing marginal utility law of diminishing marginal utility

A fundamental economic concept stating that as a product is consumed more within a given period, the additional utility obtained from it will gradually decrease.

open economy open economy

An economy that trades with the outside world to a considerable degree and establishes relations with it.

Open inflation targeting explicit inflation targeting

A monetary policy regime in which the central bank determines, under explicit rules, how it will use monetary policy instruments to achieve its inflation target.

Open expense explicit cost

Expenses incurred directly in the course of economic activity and involving a specific payment.

Open Letter Open Letter

A written text in which, pursuant to Article 42 of the CBRT Law, if inflation targets are not achieved or the possibility of not achieving them arises, the reasons for this situation and the measures to be taken are notified in writing to the Government and simultaneously announced to the public. The open letter is written, under the principles of transparency and accountability, when inflation occurs at a point outside the symmetric uncertainty band defined around the point target.

Open market operation open market operation

Or in short OMO: the central bank's buying or selling of securities from or to financial institutions for the purpose of monetary policy.

Open Market Operations - OMO Open Market Operations - OMO

Within the framework of the targets of monetary policy, the CBRT's transactions — in exchange for Turkish lira — of outright purchase and sale of securities, sale with a repurchase commitment (repo), purchase with a resale commitment (reverse repo), and the taking and giving of Turkish lira deposits, with the aim of effectively regulating the money supply and the liquidity of the economy. Through open market operations, central banks ensure that short-term interest rates form around the policy rate(s) and regulate liquidity in the financial markets.

Open Position Short Position

The part of the assets held in a financial instrument such as foreign currency, gold or securities that cannot be met by liabilities of the same kind. For example, if 5 million US dollars of assets are held against a 10 million US dollar liability, the remaining 5 million US dollars represents the open US dollar position.

Short Sale Transaction Short Selling

The transaction in which an investor sells an asset not held in its portfolio, for various reasons chief among them the expectation of a price decline, and delivers the asset by buying it from the market when the delivery time arrives.

Network effect network effect

The phenomenon of a product's value increasing as more people use it.

Excessive wealth excessive wealth

Although there is no precise definition, the state of holding wealth a thousand times or more above the average in a given society.

Overconfidence Overconfidence bias

An investor's overestimating its forecasting ability and the quality of its information; it manifests itself as excessive trading, insufficient diversification and high risk.

B

Banka paniği bank panic

Or a bank run: the desire of a large number of depositors to withdraw their deposits from a bank at the same time.

Banka parası bank money

Payment instruments held and tracked as account records by the banking system.

Bankacılık sistemi banking system

A network of institutions with a regular structure, consisting of the banks operating in a country.

Bankalararası faiz oranı interbank offered rate

Or in short IBOR, the interest rate banks pay one another for uncollateralized daily borrowing in the money market.

Bankalararası Kart Merkezi - BKM Interbank Card Center - ICC

A payment system with legal personality, established in 1990 through the partnership of 13 public and private Turkish banks to provide the clearing and settlement of debit and credit cards. Through BKM, banks carry out the clearing and settlement of the credit card and debit card payments they make on one another's behalf. BKM operates on a netting basis, and the settlement of the debts arising from netting takes place through the accounts held at the Istanbul Branch of the CBRT.

Bankalararası Para Piyasası Interbank Money Market

The market operating within the CBRT where banks can carry out TL Deposit Purchase-Sale Transactions with one another and with the CBRT, and — with only the CBRT as counterparty — Late Liquidity Window and Intraday Limit Transactions.

Bankalararası TL Aktarım Sistemi Interbank Payment System

As a component of the EFT System owned and operated by the CBRT, the system that provides the real-time electronic settlement of the payments banks make among themselves and of the banking payments related to the correspondent services they provide to financial institutions abroad.

Bankaya koşma bank run

Or a bank panic: the desire of a large number of depositors to withdraw their deposits from a bank at the same time.

Bankaya Özgü Döngüsel Sermaye Tamponu Countercyclical Capital Buffer

Refers to the additional core capital amount that banks are expected to hold, in order to prevent equity from falling short of the regulations on capital adequacy in the event that credit expansion reaches levels that can raise the general risk level of the financial sector.

Banknot Banknote

Bearing instruments that carry no interest, for which the issuing institution guarantees payment of the amount written on them to the bearer. They are legal tender. The CBRT is the only institution authorized to print Turkish lira banknotes.

Bant içinde sürünen kur crawling peg with band

An exchange rate regime in which exchange rates are allowed to move within a certain band around a central parity, and the central parity itself is changed from time to time.

Barriers to Expansion

Expansion barriers are the obstacles preventing undertakings already present in the market from increasing their market shares.

Basel Bankacılık Denetim Komitesi Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - BCBS

An international organization operating under the umbrella of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) based in Basel, Switzerland, which prepares prudential regulatory frameworks for the banking sector on a global scale. The Committee also provides cooperation on the supervision of banks. With the aim of consolidating global financial stability, the Committee issues regulatory frameworks, particularly in the fields of capital and liquidity, and monitors the implementation of these regulations in countries. The Committee submits its fundamental decisions and work programme to the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS) for approval.

Basit Faiz Oranı Simple Interest Rate

The interest rate at which an investment earns interest only on its principal during the investment period.

Basit para çarpanı simple money multiplier

The money multiplier in the case where banks hold no free reserves and the non-bank sector uses no cash.

Baskın strateji dominant strategy

In game theory, the strategy that yields a player the highest payoff regardless of the other players' strategies.

Batmasına İzin Verilemeyecek Kadar Büyük Finansal Kuruluşlar Too-Big-to-Fail

Financial institutions that carry the potential of creating systemic risk and can impose large costs on the economy should they become unable to continue their operations, owing to their size and complexity, their connections with other institutions in the financial system, and the difficulty for other financial institutions to provide their significant activities at short notice.

Baz Etkisi Base Effect

Refers to the effect carried over to the period in which the change is calculated, when the reference period for the change contains a realization significantly lower or higher than normal. For example, in calculating the annual inflation rate for November 2014, the percentage change of the November 2014 consumer index relative to the November 2013 consumer index is taken. If the consumer index rose in November 2013 at a rate far below the normal average, a base effect raising the annual inflation in November 2014 will be observed.

Baz Puan Basis Point

A unit of measurement expressing changes in interest rates. It corresponds to the fourth digit after the decimal point (0,0001). For example, if the interest rate rises from 5.25% to 6.75%, there is an increase of 150 basis points. In other words, a change of 100 basis points corresponds to a change of 1%.

Örnek: Faiz oranı 25 baz puan arttı. ( The interest rate rose by 25 basis points.)

İngilizce tanım: One hundredth of a percentage point.

break even point break even point

The point at which total revenue equals total cost, so that economic profit is zero.

free rider problem free rider problem

The situation in which some economic units use more than their share of a good or service, or do not pay the cost falling to their share.

expected value expected value

Or in short EV: the operation of taking a probability-weighted average.

Example: The expected value of the consideration was calculated from possible outcomes.( The expected value of the provision was calculated from possible outcomes.

English definition: A probability-weighted average of possible outcomes.

Expected Shortfall / CVaR Expected Shortfall / CVaR

The average loss incurred when the VaR threshold is exceeded; it measures tail risk better than VaR.

expected utility expected utility

Or in short EU: the operation of taking the probability-weighted average of utility.

Expectation Management Expectation Management

Within the monetary policy framework, expectation management is the set of strategies the CBRT applies with the aim of ensuring that the medium- and long-term inflation expectations of economic units are shaped in line with the inflation targets.

uncertainty uncertainty

The state of not knowing exactly how a future event will turn out.

Benchmarking

An undertaking's examination of the business techniques of other enterprises with high competitiveness, comparing them with its own techniques, and applying the information obtained from this comparison in its own business, with the aim of raising its competitive strength.

Beta coefficient Beta coefficient

The sensitivity of an asset's return to the market return; β=1 means moving with the market, β>1 means volatility above the market.

Human capital Human capital

; It is the accumulation related to humans such as education, skills, experience, and entrepreneurship used in production.

Bid Rigging, Collusive Bidding

( (Tendering) Cartels formed by enterprises to raise prices, share quantities or regions, or reduce the quality of goods or services for buyers who want to obtain products or services through a tender process. Cartel members operate the cartel through methods such as determining the order of winning, sharing tenders among themselves, and giving shares to losers by the artificially winning bidder.

Big Data

Big data refers to large-volume data sets that cannot be analyzed by traditional information methods and require new solutions to be processed, that can generally be produced in large quantities within a short time, that are collected from different sources, and that can contain structured or unstructured data. With the valuable insights it provides, big data gives an undertaking the opportunity to better analyze consumer preferences and behaviors, thereby enabling innovative and high-quality

Compound Interest Compound interest

The interest applied to the total amount obtained after the interest amount accruing to an investor's principal held at the bank is added to the principal.

Compound Interest Rate Compound Interest Rate

The interest reflecting the return obtained when the interest earned by an investment over the investment period is reinvested along with the principal. In other words, interest earning interest.

"Bir Hafta Vadeli Repo Faiz Oranı" "One-week Repo Rate"

In May 2010, the CBRT introduced the one-week repo interest rate as a new liquidity instrument.

"Bir hafta vadeli repo ihale faiz oranı" "one week repo auction rate"

The interest rate applied for the transaction in which banks sell the securities they hold to the CBRT for one week and buy them back at maturity.

"Bireysel arz" "individual supply"

Or in short s: the quantity of a product that a single seller in the market wants to sell, depending on different prices, in a given period.

"Bireysel talep" "individual demand"

Or in short d: the quantity of a product that a single buyer in the market wants to purchase, depending on different prices, in a given period.

"Birikmiş Faiz" "Accrued Interest"

The interest accumulated on an investment within the investment period, up to the payment date. For example, to purchase a government bond issued at 100 TL with a periodic 4% coupon payment every 6 months (182 days), the price to be paid 3 months later (91 days) is 102 TL, under the assumption that the market interest rate has not changed.

Birim esnek ilişki unit elastic relationship

A one percent increase in one variable resulting in a one percent response in the other variable.

Birim İşgücü Maliyeti Unit Labour Cost

Refers to the average labor expenditures required to produce one unit of output. It is calculated by dividing total wage payments by production. It can also be expressed as the ratio of hourly wages to labor productivity. An increase in hourly wages raises unit labor cost, while an increase in productivity lowers it. From the firm's perspective, an increase in unit labor cost is a factor that reduces profitability and weakens competitiveness.

Birinci derece fiyat ayrımcılığı first degree price discrimination

Or perfect price discrimination: the practice of selling a given product to each buyer at the highest price that buyer is willing to pay for it.

Birinci fiyat kapalı teklif ihalesi first-price sealed-bid auction

A type of auction in which participants submit sealed bids and the highest bidder wins and pays the price it bid.

Birincil Gelir Hesabı Primary Income Account

Shows the incomes obtained in return for providing labor, financial or natural resources, and the amounts paid; it includes employees' wages as well as investment income and expenditure related to direct investments, portfolio investments and other investments.

Birincil Piyasa Primary Market

The market where first-time issuances take place. The first launch (sale) of an investment instrument, for example a security, is a primary market transaction. Likewise, the auction-based sale of government domestic debt securities by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye is also a primary market transaction. Subsequent purchases and sales of these securities among investors take place in markets known as the secondary market.

Birleşme merger

The coming together of two firms of their own will to form a single new firm.

Birlikte arz edilen mallar goods in joint supply

Each of the multiple products obtained as output at the end of the same production process.

Biyokütle

A renewable energy source defined as the mass that plant or animal organisms possess at a given time.

Block Exemption

Used to describe the regulations granting exemption to certain types of agreements as a group. In Turkish competition law, these regulations are made through block exemption communiqués. Agreements within the scope of a block exemption are exempt from the prohibitions on restrictive agreements, provided they satisfy the conditions relating to the block exemption. Such agreements are automatically valid and enforceable.

Bolluk çelişkisi paradox of plenty

Or the resource curse: the phenomenon of natural resources such as oil bringing conflict, war, corruption and poverty instead of economic growth in some countries.

Bono Bill

Securities with a maturity of less than one year, for which the issuing institution undertakes to pay a certain amount at the maturity it foresees. Issues with a maturity of less than one year made by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye trade under the name Treasury Bills (Hazine Bonosu). The English equivalent 'Bond' refers to instruments with maturities longer than 10 years (maximum 30 years) for US Treasury issues. Similarly, 'Note' is used for issues of 1-10 years, and 'Bill' for issues of one year or shorter.

Borç-özsermaye oranı Debt-to-Equity ratio

The ratio of total debt to equity; it shows the level of financial leverage. As the ratio rises, financial risk increases.

Example: The entity's debt-to-equity ratio remained within the covenant limits agreed with its lender.( The entity's debt-to-equity ratio remained within the covenant limits agreed with its lender.

English definition: A financial ratio measuring total liabilities against shareholders' equity, indicating financial leverage and risk.

Boycott

Agreements not to do business with certain individuals or undertakings are called boycotts, and such behavior can be prohibited, particularly when the boycotting undertakings hold market power. Group boycotts of this kind may, for example, be used in pursuit of a price-fixing agreement. Accordingly, some rivals may decide not to do business with the others unless certain conditions are met, and this will bring about an increase in price levels. Not doing business with others

Boğa Piyasası Bull Market

Refers to a market in which prices are rising.

Broker Broker

The name given to dealers who intermediate purchase and sale transactions for a certain commission, and who carry out the transactions in their own name but on behalf of the persons or institutions they represent.

Brownfield Investment

Brownfield investments are a type of foreign direct investment taking the form of buying or leasing a facility or firm that is already active. Budget: an estimation table showing the revenues to be obtained for a certain period and the expenditures planned to be made. C2C: a commerce (e-commerce) model carried out over the internet from consumer to consumer, whose English is 'Consumer to Consumer'.

Brüt kâr marjı Gross profit margin

The ratio of gross profit (sales minus cost of goods sold) to sales; it measures cost-of-production discipline.

Buhran ya da depresyon depression

Although there is no precise definition, a severe and prolonged recession affecting multiple countries, in which total output falls by more than 10 percent.

Business

Refers to the transfer of the right to operate the facilities of undertakings by real and/or legal persons for certain periods and under certain conditions, and to carry out the marketing and distribution of the products, if any.

Bölge Kalkınma İdaresi

Corporate structures with legal personality that operate for the development of the region they are responsible for, increasing its competitiveness and reducing development gaps. In our country there are 4 Regional Development Administrations: the Eastern Anatolia Project (DAP) Regional Development Administration, the Eastern Black Sea Project (DOKAP) Regional Development Administration, the Konya Plain Project (KOP) Regional Development Administration, and the Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP) Regional Development Administration.

Bölgesi free trade area

Organized Industrial Zones where facilities operating in the same sector group and in the sub-sectors included in that sector group are located.

inflection point inflection point

The point at which the slope of a curve turns from increasing to decreasing, or from decreasing to increasing.

budget deficit budget deficit

; the situation where a government's total revenues are less than its total expenditures during a certain period and the amount of this shortfall.

budget balance budget balance

In the macroeconomic context, the difference between the state's total revenues and its total expenditures in the same period.

budget line budget line

A graphical tool showing the combinations of goods and services that can be purchased with the same fixed expenditure.

budget surplus budget surplus

; the situation where a government's total revenues are more than its total expenditures during a certain period and the amount of this excess.

Great Depression Great Depression

The period of severe economic crisis that began in the United States in 1929 and affected the whole world until the end of the 1930s.

law of large numbers law of large numbers

A fundamental statistical concept stating that when a random event is repeated many times, the average outcome will approach the expected value.

C

current current

An economics and accounting term meaning valid or in force.

GDP at current prices GDP in current prices

Or nominal GDP: the national income method measuring the value of the goods and services produced in a given period at the prices of the same period.

Current account balance current account balance

The main item in the balance of payments showing trade and income flows.

Current Exchange Rate Current Exchange Rate

Refers to the rate used in the purchase and sale of foreign currency in the foreign exchange markets, settled on the same day.

Current ratio Current ratio

The ratio of current assets to short-term liabilities; being above 1 shows that short-term debts can be covered by current assets.

CE Certificate

Under the European Union's new approach directives, a document that must be complied with for certain products, showing that products sold within the European Community are inspected according to minimum safety, health and environmental protection requirements. CIF: an abbreviation of 'Cost, Insurance and Freight', referring to the delivery term in which the cost of the goods, insurance and freight expenses are borne by the seller. Ciro (turnover): the amount an enterprise obtains within a certain period before its expenses and costs are deducted

Chamberlin model Chamberlin model

An oligopoly model in which two identical firms producing a homogeneous product make their output choices being aware of their mutual interdependence.

Chicago School

According to the view of academics, most of them from the University of Chicago, the goal of competition laws should be the protection of consumers rather than the protection of rival undertakings. Accordingly, vertical agreements and price discrimination can be excused as they do not harm consumers, while cartels leading to price fixing and market sharing, mergers creating monopoly, and dominant undertakings applying predatory prices should be subject to scrutiny. According to the Chicago School, in matters outside these

Coase theorem Coase theorem

A mathematical demonstration showing that in cases where transaction costs are low, the parties can eliminate the externality problem by reaching an agreement.

Collective Dominance

Joint dominance is a legal concept without a direct economic counterpart. In general, it is thought that joint dominance occurs in markets where there are few large undertakings that can coordinate their behavior with tacit cooperation in order to keep prices above competitive levels. For this reason, explicit coordination is not necessary. Successful cooperation requires not only alignment in prices and product levels, but also

Comity

A term of international cooperation relating to competition policies. In the case of negative comity, each country party to the international cooperation undertakes to take into account the important interests of other countries when applying its own competition law. In the case of positive comity, the relevant authority in country A requests the competition authority of country B to act on anticompetitive practices existing in country B that significantly affect market conditions in country A

Common Cost

General expenses are the costs that arise when an undertaking produces more than one product but cannot be attributed directly to the production of a single product. When production of one of these products ends, the undertaking cannot rid itself of its general expenses. It is possible to divide general expenses into common costs and operating expenses. A common cost is the cost that arises when multiple products are produced in a single production process. For example, crude oil is a common cost for these products, since both fuel oil and gasoline are produced from it

Competition Advocacy

Competition advocacy comprises the initiatives of competition authorities, in addition to enforcing competition rules, essentially through relations with other public institutions and by raising public awareness of the benefits of competition, aimed at establishing a competitive environment and increasing competition. Many activities can be regarded as competition advocacy. For example, giving opinions on current legislation or draft legislation, and on state interventions that could encourage practices restricting competition

Competition Economics

The economic analyses used in the enforcement of competition rules. In the early periods, when only legal assessments were made in competition rules, the necessity of the economic analysis of market conditions and of consumer and firm behavior came to be accepted over time. Within this framework, economic and econometric studies are used in the interpretation and enforcement of competition rules.

Competition for the Market

Seen in innovative markets with network effects and in tender markets. In innovative markets, when products are not compatible with one another, standards come to the fore. Competition concerns consumers first preferring a standard and, subsequently, owing to network effects, obtaining a large part of the market. What matters here is consumers' choices. If, with a good marketing tactic, consumers are convinced that one standard is better, the market

Competition Law

The rules concerning the preservation of competition. These rules contain the regulations necessary to establish and preserve an effective competitive environment in systems where the market economy, and hence free competition, is embraced. The prevention of agreements among undertakings, decisions of undertaking associations and practices that obstruct, distort or restrict competition, and the prevention of the abuse of dominance by undertakings dominant in the market; the review of merger or acquisition transactions for the establishment of competition in the markets

Competition Test (SLC Test)

Another of the competition-based tests used in the control of concentrations, besides the dominance test, is the 'Substantial Lessening of Competition Test' (SLC Test). The difference between the two tests stems from the difference of approach to the causes of the anticompetitive effects of mergers, rather than the effects themselves. In the SLC test, a substantial lessening of competition occurs through the creation of market power or the strengthening of existing market power, while in the dominance test, the creation of a dominant position

Competitive Price

The price formed in a market free of market failures and violations of competition, where supply and demand are determined freely. This price is expected to be close to the marginal cost and the marginal revenue.

Concession

The granting to private-law persons of the right to operate certain assets owned by the public or to carry out certain public services.

Consortium

A group of independent undertakings working together to carry out a specific project. It arises in cases involving large projects, such as the construction market, requiring close cooperation among many undertakings.

Consumer Welfare

Refers to the individual benefits consumers obtain from the consumption of goods and services. Individual welfare is defined theoretically as the individual assessments individuals make about their own satisfaction. Therefore, for consumer welfare to be measured exactly, individual preferences must be known exactly. In practice, the concept of consumer surplus is used to measure consumer welfare. Total consumer welfare is the consumer surplus for all consumers

Convergence

Refers to the bringing together of two or more unrelated economic activities in order to increase efficiency in the organization of the production process or in the market structure. The use of the fiber optic infrastructure capacity established in the energy sector also for the provision of telecommunication services is an example of convergence.

Core Principles for Effective

Banking Supervision: the Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision published by the Basel Committee in 1997. The 15th of the 25 fundamental principles published relates to money laundering. According to this principle, the institutions authorized in banking supervision should ensure that banks have sufficient and appropriate policies, including the 'know your customer' principle, that secure high ethical standards in the financial sector and prevent banks from being misused by criminals

Cournot modeli Cournot model

A duopoly model in which two identical firms producing a homogeneous product make their output choices independently of each other and simultaneously.

Coğrafi İşaret

Signs indicating a product that has become identified with a locality, area, region or country where it originates, in respect of its distinctive quality, reputation or other characteristics.

Cross Licensing

A cross-licensing agreement is a type of agreement in which two or more patent-owning undertakings grant licenses to one another or to a third party. Despite the pro-competitive aspects of such an agreement structure, such as the reduction of transaction costs and the bringing together of complementary technologies, in certain cases they can have restrictive effects on competition.

Çalışan "employed"

Or the employed: the persons engaged, in a given period, in any activity directed toward production or the provision of services with the aim of earning a wage or profit.

Çalışma İzni

The permit document drawn up in the form of an official document by the Ministry of Family, Labor and Social Services, granting foreigners, within its validity period, the right to work and reside in Türkiye.

Çalışma çağındaki nüfus working age population

According to the definition widely used in Türkiye and many countries, the population covering individuals aged 15 and over.

Çapalama etkisi Anchoring bias

The investor's attaching too much weight to the first number it sees in its evaluation (the purchase price, the peak price); it can shadow the current information regarding the target price.

Çapraz döviz kuru cross exchange rate

The exchange rate calculated between two foreign currencies using a third currency.

"Çapraz fiyat esnekliği" "cross price elasticity"

Or the cross price elasticity of demand, in short εXP: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of one related product changes as a result of a one percent increase in another product's price.

"Çapraz Kur" "Cross Rate"

In the international markets, since exchange rates are generally expressed as the rate of exchange between the US dollar and the local currencies, the rate of exchange between two currencies other than the US dollar can be calculated indirectly according to their prices in US dollars. The cross rate is the exchange rate defined as the parity between two foreign currencies and each of these two currencies with a third foreign currency (usually the US dollar). In other words, the indirect rate of exchange between two currency units is called the cross rate.

"Çarpan" "multiplier"

The coefficient showing how much effect a unit change in autonomous expenditures will have on equilibrium income.

"Çekirdek Enflasyon" "Core Inflation"

The permanent component of inflation stripped of temporary or one-off effects. Excluding certain items from the index, statistical analysis and model-based methods are frequently used in calculating core inflation; however, the most widely followed core inflation indicators are those obtained by the exclusion method. For this purpose, energy prices, basic food prices and indirect taxes, which are more exposed to external effects (energy prices, seasonal conditions, fiscal policy, etc.) and can be temporary in nature, are the main elements excluded from such inflation calculations. The purpose of using core inflation is to identify the elements that make the change in the general price level persistent. Although the inflation target is set on headline CPI inflation, the course of core inflation indicators is also taken into account so that more realistic policy decisions can be taken. In particular, in countries moving toward inflation targeting, rather than a single core inflation indicator, alternative indices calculated in different ways are followed, considering the advantages and disadvantages of all calculation methods.

"Çekirdek Yükümlülükler" "Core Liabilities"

The deposit-based funding that the banking sector obtains from savholders domestically is generally called core liabilities. Since core liabilities grow in proportion to the economy's size and the household's wealth, they are accepted as a source compatible with the economy's fundamentals for banks' credit expansion. In the credit expansion periods in which credits grow faster than deposits, banks can turn to non-core liabilities and thereby feed the macro-financial vulnerabilities in the financial system.

"Çerçeveleme etkisi" "Framing effect"

The production of different decisions according to the manner of presentation of the same option (as a gain or as a loss); 'a 90% chance of survival' and 'a 10% risk of death' are the same thing.

"Çevrimsel bütçe dengesi" "cyclical budget balance"

The deficit or surplus realized in the public budget balance depending on the business cycles.

"Çevrimsel işsizlik" "cyclical unemployment"

The type of unemployment arising as a result of the fall in total production in the economy because of the business cycles.

"Çift taraflı tekel" "bilateral monopoly"

A market structure in which there is a single buyer corresponding to a single seller.

"Çok-birimli ihale" "multi-unit auction"

The offering for sale, by auction, of more than one product at once.

Çoklu Bölge Fiyatlandırması Sistemi

( Multiple Zone Pricing System): Under this method, the same delivery price is applied to all buyers in a zone, while prices differ between zones.

Çözümleme Resolution

The subjection of a financial institution, as a result of the relevant authorities' establishing that it no longer possesses the capital necessary for it to be able to continue its activities, to a special intervention, with the aim of its liquidation, or of its being restored to the capital structure it needs in order to be able to continue its activities.

Çıktı Açığı Output Gap

The output gap, defined as the difference of the output realized in an economy from its potential level, is an important monetary policy variable in the evaluation of the price pressures in the economy. Under the inflation targeting regime, central banks shape their policies according to the forward-looking inflation expectations rather than realized inflation. Accordingly, in the areas where the output gap is positive, it is estimated that the economy is operating above capacity because of the demand surplus, and that this can cause demand-side inflationary pressure. In contrast, in the areas where the output gap is negative, it is estimated that there is a supply surplus or idle capacity stemming from the weak demand in the economy, and that this too can cause a fall in inflation.

Çıktı piyasası output market

Or the product market: the markets where the goods and services directed toward final consumption are bought and sold.

Çıktı-faktör eğrisi output-factor curve

Or the expansion path: a graphical tool showing how the factor bundles used by the producer change as total product increases, all else being constant.

Çıpa Nominal Anchor

It is used to express the magnitudes taken as reference in the economic decision-making processes. For example, the concept of the exchange rate anchor expresses that, following a central bank's making certain commitments for the exchange rate, and with the other economic units also trusting this commitment, the changes in the exchange rate are taken as the basis in the economic decisions taken, and the decisions such as price, wage increase and investment take shape within the framework of the exchange rate policy. In the absence of trust in such an anchor (policy), the selected magnitudes lose these properties. The monetary magnitudes, interest rates, inflation and growth rates are the magnitudes used as 'anchors'. Particularly in recent years, the difficulties arising in the use of magnitudes such as the exchange rate and the interest rate as anchors have generalized the use of inflation for this purpose.

An exchange rate regime in which nominal exchange rates are freely determined by foreign currency supply and demand in the foreign exchange market.

Refers to the estimation, by economic methods, of the harm suffered by consumers or customers owing to undertakings' practices in cartel or abuse-of-dominance investigations. In the analysis, fundamentally, the price and quantity levels that could have formed in the market had the infringing practice not existed are compared with the price and quantity levels actually observed, and the welfare loss caused by the difference is assessed.

The case where, while all production factors increase at the same rate, the quantity of output increases less than the increase rate of the production factors. Hence the rate of increase in output is smaller compared to the increase in input quantity. In this case, as the quantity produced rises, long-run average cost increases.

Refers to a continuous fall in the general level of prices.

In sectors where transportation costs are significant, if sellers and buyers are dispersed across regions far from one another, final prices can differ substantially. In such sectors, if the product is homogeneous and demand elasticity is low, undertakings seeking agreement on price setting can overcome this problem with 'delivered pricing'. There are various delivered pricing arrangements: Single Basing Point System: for this method to be applied, the primary

The first derivative of the option price with respect to the price of the underlying asset (Δ = ∂C/∂S = N(d1)); in Black-Scholes, the delta hedge is constructed with this ratio.

The exchange rate at which purchase and sale transactions take place when the foreign exchange market is in equilibrium.

The interest rate at which borrowing and lending transactions take place when the money market is in equilibrium.

equilibrium quantity equilibrium quantity

equilibrium fee equilibrium wage

Products are differentiated by undertakings with the aim of selling at a higher price and/or increasing sales. Differentiation can be based on physical appearance, quality, durability, tied services (warranties, after-sales services and information), image and geographic location. When a product is differentiated,

Dikey birleşme vertical merger

The merger of two firms relating to different parts or production stages of a certain product or product group.

Diligence (on New Technologies)

The diligence due from financial institutions so that new technologies are not used as a tool in money laundering. Accordingly, financial institutions should exercise special care against new and advanced technologies that pose a money laundering danger by concealing identity information, and take the measures necessary to prevent these technologies from being used for money laundering purposes; in particular, they should have policies and procedures identifying the risks for business relations and transactions not carried out face to face

Dip trough

Divestiture Trustee

The person appointed by the parties with the aim of continuously monitoring, on behalf of the competition authority until the closing of the transaction, whether the commitments accepted in merger or acquisition decisions are being complied with, and of contributing to the implementations. Diğer her şey sabit all else being equal

Dolarizasyon Dolarization / Currency Substitution

The use by residents of a country of foreign currency instead of their own national currency as a medium of exchange, unit of account and store of value. Full dollarization is a country's completely abandoning its national currency and adopting a foreign currency as its official currency. Partial dollarization arises when economic units in a country, in an environment of high inflation and uncertainty, begin to prefer financial assets in foreign currency instead of financial assets in national currency, in order to protect themselves from the possible loss of value of the national currency. It is generally observed that the first stage of dollarization develops as 'asset substitution', the beginning of the use of foreign-currency assets as a store of value. On the other hand, the banking crises frequently experienced in the recent past, particularly in emerging markets, have added to the economics literature the concept of 'liability dollarization' in addition to asset dollarization. Liability dollarization is the holding of large amounts of foreign-currency liabilities by all economic units in the country, including the banking and public sectors. Both asset and liability dollarization can be gathered under a single heading and characterized as 'financial dollarization'. Financial dollarization is defined as the tendencies of residents of a country to hold both their assets and their liabilities in foreign currency.

direct tax direct tax

natural rate of unemployment natural rate of unemployment

natural resource natural resource

natural monopoly natural monopoly

One of the open market operations the CBRT uses, within the framework of its monetary policy targets, with the aim of effectively regulating the money supply and the liquidity of the economy. "Doğrudan (Kesin) Satım" "Outright Sale"

"Doğrudan alım" "outright purchase"

The transaction of the central bank purchasing securities in the open market.

"Doğrudan kotasyon" "direct quotation"

Or in short E: the exchange rate showing how much domestic currency can be bought in exchange for one unit of foreign currency.

"Doğrudan müdahale" "direct intervention"

The practices by which the state influences the market through price or quantity regulation.

"Doğrudan satım" "outright sale"

The transaction of the central bank selling securities in the open market.

"Örnek: Varlık, kesin bir satış yoluyla devredildi. "( "The asset was transferred through an outright sale.)"

A long-term form of investment in which the investor controls the management of an enterprise, or has a say in its management, in an economy other than the one where it is resident. "Due Diligence"

Due Diligence is the analysis containing all the necessary financial, legal and administrative information required for an investment decision to be made, showing the company's current situation and enabling the most accurate forecasts about its future. Fixed Assets: business assets that do not have the property of being converted into cash within one year.

"Duopol" "duopoly"

A market structure in which there are only two sellers of a good. Each producer generally has to take into account the other's reaction regarding any change it will make in price or production quantity. Since competition is between only two firms, their degrees of interdependence are quite high.

"DuPont analizi" "DuPont analysis"

The analysis that breaks return on equity (ROE) into three components: ROE = Net Profit Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier. It shows which item is dragging down profitability; not fabricated terms like 'profit multiplier' or the like.

Duran varlık fixed asset

Or fixed capital: durable goods such as machinery, factories, vehicles and buildings produced to generate income in the future.

Örnek: Yeni makine duran varlık olarak kaydedilir. ( The new machine is recorded as a fixed asset.)

Dönemsel Faiz Periodic Interest Rate

Refers to the interest an investment will yield over the period it is actually held.

Dördüncü derece fiyat ayrımcılığı fourth degree price discrimination

Or reverse price discrimination: the practice of selling a given product to each buyer at the same price even though its cost differs for different buyers.

Döviz foreign exchange

The currencies of foreign countries or any payment instruments substituting for foreign currency.

Döviz arz eğrisi foreign exchange supply curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the exchange rate and the quantity of foreign currency supplied, all else being constant.

Döviz arzı foreign exchange supply

Or in short SE: the total quantity of foreign currency that all units in the economy want to sell, depending on the exchange rate, in a given period.

Döviz Kuru Exchange Rate

The expression of one national currency in terms of another national currency.

Exchange rate targeting exchange rate targeting
