For central banks, independence mostly expresses instrument independence.

Merkez Bankası Bağımsızlığı Central Bank Independence

The capacity of the monetary authorities to take their institutional, administrative, financial and monetary policy-related decisions independently of any element of pressure.

Merkez Bankası Müdahalesi Central Bank Intervention

The making of purchases and sales by central banks in the markets, directed toward realizing their short- and long-term monetary policy aims. With the intervention, the aim is to lower/raise the market prices of the variables intervened in, such as exchange rates and interest, to the levels foreseen in the policy. Intervention methods can differ. Central banks can intervene directly and openly by being counterparty and showing themselves, or they can intervene indirectly. Similarly, central bank interventions can be announced in advance in terms of time and amount, or can be carried out without any announcement. The situations requiring intervention take shape within the framework of the monetary policy aims being implemented.

Merkezi Karşı Taraf - MKT Central Counterparty - CCP

The organization undertaking the completion of transactions by assuming the role of buyer against seller and seller against buyer among the parties of the financial contracts traded in one or more markets.

Merkezi Kayıt Kuruluşu - MKK Central Registry Agency - CRA

The central registration and depository institution operating to carry out the transactions relating to the book-entry registration of capital market instruments, to track by book entry, electronically, these registered instruments and the rights attached to them by members and rights holders, and to carry out their central depository. At present, the share certificates of the companies whose shares trade on Borsa Istanbul, exchange-traded funds, investment funds, government domestic debt securities, private sector debt instruments, asset-backed securities and lease certificates are tracked by book entry by MKK. The clearing and settlement of the purchase and sale transactions relating to those of the said capital market instruments tracked by book entry at MKK that trade on Borsa Istanbul is carried out through the integrated system between MKK and Takasbank. The settlement of the said transactions realized on Borsa Istanbul is completed when the transfer of the securities in the investors' accounts at MKK takes place, in line with the customer-based netted transaction results received from Takasbank. Within this scope, for the untroubled realization of the clearing and settlement of the purchase and sale transactions of the said capital market instruments traded on Borsa Istanbul, the MKK system must operate in coordination with Takasbank's system.

Merkezi planlamalı ekonomi centrally planned economy

The economic system in a country in which the state decides what to produce, how, and for whom.

Merkezi Saklama Kuruluşu Central Securities Depository

The institutions possessing private-law legal personality in the form of joint-stock companies that provide the services of the central depository of capital market instruments and the exercise of the rights relating to them.

Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Dengesi Central Government Budget Balance

The budget balance found by subtracting budget expenditures from the total of the budget revenues of the general budget administrations, special budget administrations and regulatory and supervisory institutions within the scope of central government.

Merkezi Yönetim Bütçesi Central Government Budget

; The main budget title consists of three parts: General Budget, Special Budget, and Budget of Regulatory and Supervisory Agencies.

Merkezi Yönetim Faiz Dışı Bütçe Dengesi Central Government Primary Budget Balance

The budget balance found by subtracting the non-interest budget expenditures from the total of the budget revenues of the general budget administrations, special budget administrations and regulatory and supervisory institutions within the scope of central government.

Merkezi Yönetim Riski Sovereign Risk

Refers to the risk an investor is exposed to because of lending to a country other than the one where it is resident, or lending to an institution/organization guaranteed by the government of the said country. Risks such as the reduction of the value of foreign-currency liabilities by the alteration of exchange rate regulations by the central bank or competent authority of the country invested in, or the non-realization of direct debt or interest payments, constitute sovereign risk.

Mevduat bankası deposit bank

The institutions that collect deposits in return for interest, extend credits, and offer various financial services.

Mevduat oranı deposit rate

The interest rate banks give in return for the deposits they collect.

Adjustment for Seasonal and Calendar Effects Adjustment for Seasonal and Calendar Effects

The periodic movements repeating in the same periods of every year can be called seasonality. The calendar effect, on the other hand, includes the movements that can form due to effects such as the change in the number of working days in a period. In order to better evaluate the tendencies in the data and to compare consecutive periods, series are adjusted for seasonality and calendar effects by statistical methods.

Micro Enterprise

The enterprises employing fewer than ten annual employees and whose annual net sales revenue or financial balance sheet, whichever applies, does not exceed three million Turkish liras.

Microeconomics microeconomics

The main branch of economics that takes the decision-makers in the economy individually and examines their behavior.

Microfinance microfinance

The small-scale banking and insurance services provided to persons having difficulty accessing the traditional financial system.

Microcredit microcredit

The credits given for low-income individuals and, particularly, women to engage in a production activity that will sustain themselves.

Quantity restriction quantity restriction

The market intervention the state implements by determining the quantity supplied for a product.

National income accounting national income accounting

The general name of the methods such as gross domestic product, gross national product, net national product, personal income and disposable personal income, used to track total production and total income in the economy.

fundamental identity of national income accounting fundamental identity of national income accounting

The fact that the market value of total production in a country, the total expenditure made to purchase these products, and the total income arising from sales equal one another.

Minimum Efficient Scale

The minimum efficient scale is the smallest scale at which average costs are minimized. This concept carries importance for understanding market structure. For example, in the case where the minimum efficient scale is smaller compared to the general size of the market, a greater number of firms is expected to be found in the market, and hence the market is expected to have a competitive structure.

Model model

The whole of the mathematical definitions and relationships serving to describe and predict an economic phenomenon or behavior by simplifying it to a certain extent.

Model Factory

The training applications specially designed — and the physical environments where these applications will be offered — to develop the application-oriented skills of enterprises, through learning by doing in experimental settings, on matters such as lean production, process improvement, product development and problem solving, within the scope of the efficiency increase and digitalization required for global competition in enterprises, and to transform firms by quickly putting these new skills into practice.

Modern miktar kuramı modern quantity theory

The body of principles maintaining that, under the assumption of the stability of the velocity of money's circulation, there is a same-directional and proportional relationship between the money supply and the general price level.

Modernization Investment

Refers to the investments including the addition of parts suited to the machinery and equipment that have completed their technical and/or economic life in the production lines of existing facilities, or the replacement of existing machinery and equipment with new ones, the completion of the sections left incomplete in the facility, the direct raising of the quality of the final product or the changing of its model.

Modified duration Modified duration

The sensitivity measure, found by dividing the Macaulay duration by (1+y), giving the percentage effect on the price of a one-unit change in interest: ΔP ≈ −D*·Δy.

Money Laundering and Terrorist

Financing. IBAN (International Bank Account Number): the International Bank Account Number providing the standard for the automatic holding and validity of bank account numbers. IBAN, developed by ECBS (European Committee for Banking Standards), is a series of alphanumeric characters identifying an account held at a bank anywhere in the world. Having at most 34 characters, IBAN contains the ISO, the country code, two check digits and the bank account number. Processed and stored electronically

Monopol monopoly

A monopoly is the situation in which there is a single seller in the market. The demand curve facing the monopolist is negatively sloped. The comparison of the outcomes of the monopoly and fully competitive markets shows that the monopolist sets a higher price, produces less, and earns more than economic profit (monopoly rent). In this case, consumers face a high price in a way that causes a loss of welfare, and income flows from consumers to the monopolist undertaking

Monopson monopsony

A market structure in which a product supplied by more than one seller is demanded by a single buyer, and obstacles lie before the entry of other buyers into the market.

Moratoryum Moratorium

A debtor's declaring that it will be unable to pay all or a part of its debts owing to losing its ability to pay. It generally results in the restructuring of the debt between the debtor and the creditor.

Mortgage

A long-term investment instrument offering persons who do not have enough savings to own a home the opportunity to become homeowners by making monthly low installments, as if making rent payments.

Muhasebe kârı accounting profit

The profit calculation taking into account only the explicit expenses.

Mutabakat Settlement

The fulfillment of the obligations arising from the transfer of funds or securities between two or more parties.

Örnek: Yükümlülüğün ödenmesi izleyen dönemde gerçekleşti. ( Settlement of the obligation occurred in the following period.

English definition: Extinguishing a liability by paying or transferring resources.

"Mutlak yoksulluk" "absolute poverty"

; "en temel gıda, temizlik, sağlık ve eğitim hizmetlerini karşılayabilecek kadar gelire sahip olmama durumudur."

"Mutlak yoksulluk oranı" "absolute poverty rate"

The ratio of the population living below the poverty line in a country to the total population.

"Mübadele denklemi" "equation of exchange"

The fundamental equation stating that the product of the money supply and the velocity of money's circulation equals nominal GDP.

"Müşteriler Arası TL Aktarım Sistemi" "Retail Payment System"

As a component of the EFT System owned and operated by the CBRT, the system providing the real-time electronic settlement of the payments banks carry out on behalf of their customers, such as account-based and name-based customer payments, public payments, housing, workplace and other rent payments, salary and credit card payments.

N

"NAIRU ya da enflasyonu artırmayan işsizlik oranı" nonaccelarating inflation rate of unemployment

The unemployment rate that keeps a country's labor market in long-run equilibrium and therefore does not lead to an increase in inflation.

Nakliye Eşitleme Sistemi (Freight

Equalization System): This method fundamentally resembles the multiple basing point system; the only difference is that all the production centers are accepted as basing points. Hence sellers calculate the delivered price as if the sale were to be made from the nearest rival to the buyer.

Nash dengesi Nash equilibrium

The situation reached in game theory as a result of each player's choosing its own best strategy according to its predictions about the other players' strategies.

Nazım İmar Planı

The term for the master plan reports showing all the particulars of lands with determined cadastral status on plans at a scale of 1/2000 or 1/5000, prepared in a manner consistent with the environment or regional order plans. Master plans are created to show the uses of lands, the zone types, the population structure and the transportation systems. All these points are stated in a detailed report. The master plans show what form a settlement area will take in the future.

Negatif dışsallık negative externality

The adverse effect an economic activity has on persons who are not party to that activity.

Negatif çıktı açığı negative output gap

Or a recessionary gap: the situation in which, in the short run, real GDP is below potential GDP, and hence the economy is considered to be in a contraction period.

Net Bugünkü Değer Net Present Value

The value reached as a result of the return provided by an investment over the investment period being discounted, brought to the present, with the market interest rate or its own interest rate.

Net factor income net factor income

The difference between the revenues domestic production factors obtain abroad and the revenues foreign production factors obtain domestically.

Net Hata ve Noksan Net Errors and Omission

Because the balance of payments is an accounting system in which every transaction is recorded with two separate signs (a credit and a debit entry), it is essential that, while each transaction of the balance of payments is recorded under the item relating to its content, its counterpart entry takes place in another item. In other words, every transaction being recorded with equal-value credit and debit entries requires that the total of the 'Current Accounts' and the 'Capital Account' always equal the 'Financial Account' item. However, the obtaining of the data from different sources creates differences in valuation, measurement and recording time; the differences formed as a result are reflected as a 'residual' in the Net Errors and Omissions item. This item is obtained by subtracting the current account and the capital account from the financial account.

Net ihracat net exports

Or in short NX: the main expenditure heading showing the difference between the products the domestic economic units export to the outside world and the products they import from the outside world.

Net işletme sermayesi Net Working Capital

The excess of short-term assets over short-term liabilities (Current Assets − Short-Term Liabilities); it shows the liquidity buffer.

Net İstikrarlı Fonlama Oranı Net Stable Funding Ratio - NSFR

The ratio of the current steady funding amount to the required steady funding amount. The current steady funding amount fundamentally consists of capital, liabilities with an effective maturity of more than one year, and savings and SME deposits. Some other liabilities are included in steady funding after being multiplied by certain coefficients. The required steady funding amount is obtained by classifying assets, according to their liquidity, from the most liquid to the least liquid and multiplying them by certain coefficients.

Net kâr marjı Net profit margin

The ratio of net profit to sales (Net profit / Sales) and the first component of the DuPont analysis; it shows how much net profit remains from every 1 lira of sales.

Net milli hasıla net national product

Or in short NNP: the difference between all the final goods and services produced by a country's citizens in a given period and the capital spent during this production.

Net Satış Hasılatı

Refers to the amount found as a result of deducting sales discounts and returns and other rebates from an enterprise's gross sales. NUTS: The Classification of Territorial Units for Statistics (İBBS), developed since the 1970s by the Statistical Office of the European Communities (Eurostat) in order to ensure that regional statistics in the European Union are produced according to a single spatial classification

Net vergiler net taxes

The difference between the taxes households and firms pay to the state and the transfer payments the state makes to households and firms.

Netleştirme Netting

The conversion, by mutual offsetting, of the receivables and debts arising from the transfer orders a participant in a payment or securities settlement system has sent and received, into a single receivable or debt.

Network Effects

Network externality is the external benefit that each consumer joining a network provides for the other customers within the network. As the number of users increases, a certain product or service becomes more valuable in the user's eyes. This situation is also called a network externality.

Nicel Genişleme Quantitative Easing

An unconventional monetary policy approach, meaning central banks' increasing the money supply by purchasing financial assets from commercial banks or other private institutions. After the global financial crisis, the central banks of the United States in particular, and of England, Europe and Japan, applied quantitative expansion policies of different magnitudes in order to support the financial sector, increase private consumption expenditures and prevent inflation from falling below the target.

Nihai Kredi Mercii Lender of Last Resort

A concept expressing that, because of their capacity as monetary authority and their obligations to ensure financial stability, central banks are the final institution of application for participants, in the event that the funding shortages arising in the system cannot be met from the market, the participants applying to the central bank and benefiting from the facilities arranged under this name.

Nihai mal final good

The products purchased by their final user.

Nihai Yurt İçi Talep Final Domestic Demand

The total of the private and public sector consumption and investment expenditures.

Nokta esnekliği point elasticity

The elasticity calculation method used to find the elasticity at a single point on a curve or line.

Nominal Değer Par Value, Face Value

The value written on an instrument. For example, the nominal value of each government domestic debt security (DİBS) issued by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye is 100 TL, the value actually written on it. Similarly, the nominal value of a 200 TL banknote is 200, the value written on it.

Nominal döviz kuru nominal exchange rate

Or in short E: the relative value of one currency in terms of another currency.

Nominal Efektif Döviz Kuru Nominal Effective Exchange Rate

Refers to the average of the exchange rates selected in line with a certain aim, obtained using an appropriate weighting method.

Nominal faiz Nominal interest rate

The interest rate written in the contract, without inflation adjustment; it does not show the real increase in purchasing power.

Nominal faiz oranı nominal interest rate

Or in short i, the percentage borrowers pay to lenders without adjusting for price changes caused by inflation.

Nominal GSYH nominal GDP

Or GDP in current prices: the national income method measuring the value of the goods and services produced in a given period at the prices of the same period.

Nominal katılık nominal rigidity

; The phenomenon of sticky fees and prices observed in the short term due to various contracts, regulations, or other costs.

Normal mal normal good

Products whose demand in the market increases when the average income level rises.

Normatif çözümleme normative analysis

The analytical approach that treats economic behavior and systems with a subjective perspective, focuses on their consequences, and contains value judgments.

Notification

The notification is the presentation of the necessary information to the Competition Board in requests such as merger or acquisition permission, a negative clearance certificate, or the granting of an exemption.

O

Okun Yasası Okun's Law

The analysis stating that, as a result of every one percent increase in the unemployment rate, real GDP will fall by approximately two percent.

Olasılık probability

Or in short Pr: the frequency rate of seeing an outcome belonging to a random event.

Example: A provision is recognized when an outflow of resources is probable.( A provision is recognised when an outflow is probable.)

İngilizce tanım: More likely than not to occur.

Oligopol oligopoly

A market structure in which firms with large market shares are found, and these firms act with mutual interdependence in their price-output choices.

Confirmation bias Confirmation bias

A person's seeking out the information supporting their own view and ignoring the contradictory one; it leads to one-sided evidence gathering in analysis.

One-Stop Shopping

Refers to the possibility of customers' needs in different areas being met from a single service point (for example hypermarkets).

operating target operating target

The financial indicator that the central bank closely monitors in order to keep its intermediate target under control.

Option Option

Contracts granting the right to buy or sell a certain good, asset or financial indicator at a predetermined maturity and price. While the holder of the contract has the right to buy (call option) or sell (put option) the instrument underlying the contract, it has no obligation whatsoever arising from the contract. The party selling (writing) the contract, on the other hand, is obliged to fulfill the terms of the agreement if the party holding the contract wants, at maturity, to buy or sell the instrument underlying the contract within the contract's conditions. The parties selling (writing) the options obtain premium income in return for this transaction. In markets where uncertainty (volatility) is high, the premium demands for the contract can reach very high dimensions.

The holder of the call option may purchase the shares at the agreed exercise price.)( The holder of the call option may purchase the shares at the agreed exercise price.

A contract that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a specified price.

Optimum Scale

The scale permitting production and sales with the lowest possible cost.

ordinal utility ordinal utility

; the idea that the utility consumers derive from goods and services can be measured not numerically but through comparison and ranking.

Organic Farming

A production system directed at re-establishing the balance in nature lost as a result of mistaken practices, containing production systems friendly to humans and the environment by controlling diseases and pests with biological control ensuring continuity in the soil's fertility, prohibiting the use of synthetic chemical fertilizers and pesticides, recommending organic and green fertilization, crop rotation and soil conservation, every stage of which, from production to consumption, is under control, and the product obtained is documented with a certificate

Organized Industrial Zone

( TDİOSB) A region for the production of goods and services that includes plant and animal production forming agricultural-based industrial inputs and industrial facilities for the processing of these, aimed at integrating the agricultural and industrial sectors.

Derivative Markets Derivative Markets

The markets operating within the exchange in which standardized derivative transaction contracts are bought and sold forward, and the settlements carried out are guaranteed by an institution. The derivative market transactions — futures, forwards, options and swaps — can be used by market players with the aim of hedging against risk or making profit.

Midpoint formula midpoint formula

In economics, the calculation method of dividing the net change by the average change in order to find the average percentage change.

common value auction common value auction

The auction environment in which each participant assigns a value to the object of the auction depending on the others, and this value is decisive for everyone.

common resource common resource

Goods that are non-excludable in consumption but create rivalry.

tragedy of commons tragedy of commons

The economics concept describing the destruction or damaging of the common resources shared by everyone in society as a result of personal interest and greed.

average variable cost average variable cost

Or in short AVC: the variable cost incurred per unit of product.

average revenue average revenue

Or in short AR: the revenue obtained per unit of product.

average expenditure average expenditure

Or in short AE: the expenditure made per unit of product.

average fixed cost average fixed cost

Or in short AFC: the fixed cost incurred per unit of product.

average total cost average total cost

Or in short ATC: the total cost incurred per unit of product.

Bail-in Bail-in

The practice of including, in the losses arising during resolution, not only the shareholders of the financial institutions but also those providing credit to these institutions.

Automatic Stabilizers Automatic Stabilisers

The fiscal elements that function spontaneously, quickly and effectively in the establishment and maintenance of economic balance. Progressive taxes and unemployment insurance payments can be given as examples.

Automatic stabilizers automatic stabilizer

The public budget elements that come into play spontaneously with the business cycles and have a reducing effect on the fluctuations in the economy.

Autonomous variable autonomous variable

In a mathematical model, the external effects that are not dependent on the other variables.

Autonomous money demand autonomous money demand

; It is the fixed part of money demand that is not dependent on interest rate, income or general price level.

Autonomous consumption autonomous consumption

The fixed portion of private consumption expenditures not dependent on income.

Autonomous investment autonomous investment

The fixed portion of planned investments independent of income or the interest rate.

Session Permission

The other name of the residence permit that foreigners who have decided to settle in Türkiye for various reasons are obliged to obtain.

Volatility Volatility

The expression of the variability in an instrument's price. It is mostly measured with the standard deviation. High volatility is an indicator of increasing uncertainty.

Game theory game theory

The body of principles explaining how economic units, acting in line with their own interest, will behave in mutual competition or cooperation.

Player player

In game theory, the economic units whose behavior it is desired to explain.

Ö

Payment Against Delivery Principle -PAD Delivery versus Payment - DvP

The link between a securities transfer system and a funds transfer system ensuring that delivery takes place if and only if payment takes place.

Payment for Payment Payment versus Payment - PvP

The method ensuring that a transfer made in one currency takes place if and only if simultaneously with a transfer made in the other currency, in foreign exchange settlement systems.

Payment Institution Payment Institution

The legal person authorized under Law No. 6493 on Payment and Securities Settlement Systems, Payment Services and Electronic Money Institutions in order to provide and carry out payment services.

Payment System Payment System

The structure with common rules, offering the infrastructure necessary for the clearing and settlement transactions made with the aim of realizing the fund transfers arising from the transfer orders among three or more participants.

Balance of Payments Balance of Payments

A statistical report prepared in order to obtain the systematic records of the economic transactions that the resident persons in an economy (general government, central bank, banks, other sectors) have carried out, within a certain period, with the persons resident in other economies (non-residents).

Ödenti payoff

In game theory, the profit or loss a player obtains at the end of the strategy it pursues.

Ödenti matrisi payoff matrix

The table showing the different payoffs that will be obtained as a result of the different strategies that more than one player can pursue.

Ölçek ekonomisi economies of scale

The concept describing how total product is affected when all the production factors are changed at the same rate.

Ölçeğe göre artan getiri increasing returns to scale

The total product's increasing at a higher rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.

Ölçeğe göre azalan getiri decreasing returns to scale

The total product's increasing at a lower rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.

Ölçeğe göre sabit getiri constant returns to scale

The total product's increasing at the same rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.

Criterion Value Benchmark Security

It is used in the sense of a measurement and comparison criterion. For example, in portfolio management, the benchmark portfolio is the portfolio taken as the basis for measuring the performance (in the sense of return and risk) success of the portfolios formed outside this structure. Another example: benchmark securities are the instruments that have enough liquidity in the market, whose maintenance of this property by the issuing institution is in question, and that form a reference in the market for similar issues.

Pre-Project

The project containing one or several solutions in which the plan, section, view and profiles are indicated — prepared on the basis of the data obtained, including the environmental impact assessment and feasibility reports, according to the precise requirements program of a certain structure, without the necessary land and ground investigations having been made, the information being taken from the existing maps.

Priority Product List

The list prepared by the Ministry of Industry and Technology with the aim of identifying the products to be prioritized, taking into account criteria such as foreign trade data, global competitive conditions, local and global demand trends, domestic production competence and capacity, and contribution to sectoral and inter-sectoral technological development.

Leading Indicator leading indicator

The measurable factors that develop before a change is seen in the fundamental macroeconomic magnitudes such as national income and inflation.

Precautionary motive precautionary motive

The demand for money stemming from the thought of being prepared for the emergencies that may arise in the future.

Sample Banknote Specimen

The banknote whose possibility of circulation has been removed by the writing 'Örnektir Geçmez' (Sample — Not Valid) or 'Specimen' being printed or stapled on it, with the aim of introducing the banknotes to be put into circulation.

Implicit inflation targeting implicit inflation targeting

The monetary policy regime in which it is not explicit how the central bank will use the monetary policy instruments in order to achieve the inflation it targets.

Implicit cost implicit cost

The expenses that are not incurred directly during the economic activity and that contain no specific payment.

Tacit collusion tacit collusion

Firms' or states' secretly agreeing and acting in coordination in ways that benefit one another.

Private Budget Private Budget

; It is the budget of institutions established under a ministry or to carry out a specific public service, such as the Higher Education Council, Turkish Language Institution, universities, TÜBİTAK.

Special value auction private value auction

The auction environment in which each participant assigns its own value to the object of the auction, and this value is independent of the other participants.

Specific scope CPI specific coverage CPI

A price index taking as its product basket the product groups contained in the CPI with high predictive power regarding the future of inflation.

Special Scope CPI Indicators - SSCI Special CPI Aggregates - SCA

The price indices reached through the exclusion of some sub-items from the CPI. In order to be able to measure the effectiveness of the policies implemented within the framework of monetary policy, the items outside the monetary policy's control must be excluded from the CPI. However, since the shocks to inflation can be of different character by period, the probability of a single 'core inflation' indicator excluding all the elements outside monetary policy control is quite low. For this reason, instead of a single indicator that can be called core, special-scope indicators determined in ways that can assist the separation of the different external shocks are used.

Special tranche bond rate corporate bond rate

The interest rate on securities issued by private banks and corporations into the market.

Private good private good

Goods that are excludable in consumption and create rivalry.

Private consumption expenditures private consumption expenditures

Or in short C: the main expenditure heading covering the purchases of goods and services for consumption by the economic units domestically.

Special Drawing Rights Special Drawing Right- SDR

The reserve asset created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) with the aim of contributing to the member countries' existing official reserves, and allocated to the member countries in proportion to their IMF quotas.

Specific risk Unsystematic risk

The risk specific to the company/sector and eliminable with sufficient diversification; in Turkish it is also called 'unsystematic risk'.

Equity owners' equity

All the resources belonging to an organization with legal personality, such as its own money, buildings, vehicles and office equipment.

Example: Total equity increased as a result of the profit for the year and the share issue.)( Total equity increased as a result of the profit for the year and the share issue.

English definition: The residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting all of its liabilities.

Return on equity Return on Equity - ROE

The ratio of net profit to equity (Net profit / Equity); the fundamental profitability ratio measuring the profit per shareholder.

Equity multiplier Equity multiplier

The ratio of total assets to equity (Total Assets / Equity); it is the expression of financial leverage in the DuPont analysis. The term 'share segment' is wrong; the correct term is equity.

P

Money money

Any kind of object generally accepted as payment in return for goods and services.

Money supply curve money supply curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the nominal interest rate and the quantity of money in the economy, all else being constant.

Money supply money supply

Or in short MS: the quantity of money that the central bank, the commercial banks and the non-bank sector together bring into being in a given period.

Near money near money

The securities that are close substitutes for money for transaction purposes.

Currency board currency board

An exchange rate regime permitting the printing of domestic currency in a country only up to the amount of foreign currency owned.

Money Market Money Market

The market in which short-term (90 days or less for international markets), highly liquid financial instruments trade.

Money market equilibrium money market equilibrium

The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of money demanded in the market equals the quantity of money supplied.

Money market fund money market fund

Investment funds consisting of short-term, low-risk securities.

Monetary Policy Monetary Policy

Refers to the decisions taken with the aim of influencing the availability and cost of money in order to reach aims such as economic growth, increasing employment and price stability. The institutions responsible for its implementation are central banks. In the CBRT Law, it is stated that the fundamental aim of the CBRT is to ensure price stability.

Monetary Policy Committee - MPC Monetary Policy Committee - MPC

The board formed within the CBRT, charged and authorized with determining the monetary policy principles and strategies with the aim of ensuring price stability, and, within the framework of these strategies, determining the inflation target together with the government, taking the measures necessary to preserve the internal and external value of the Turkish lira, and determining, again together with the government, the exchange rate regime directed at establishing its parity against foreign currencies and gold. The Monetary Policy Committee, under the chairmanship of the Governor, consists of the Deputy Governors, a member to be elected by the Bank Council from among its members, and a member to be appointed by joint decision upon the Governor's proposal. The Undersecretary of Treasury or the Deputy Undersecretary he designates may attend the meetings without voting rights.

demand for money demand for money

Or in short MD: the quantity of money that all the units in the economy want to hold, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.

money demand curve money demand curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the nominal interest rate and the quantity of money economic units want to hold, all else being constant.

currency carry trade currency carry trade

Or in short carry trade: the transaction of making gains by borrowing in a currency yielding low interest and investing in a currency yielding high interest.

Money and Banking Statistics Money and Banking Statistics

A stock data showing the money, deposits and other monetary liabilities of the central bank and the banks, the credits extended by these institutions, and their positions vis-à-vis abroad. By the residency principle, the transactions belonging to banks' foreign organizations are not included.

money multiplier money multiplier

Or in short θ (read theta): the coefficient showing how much money will be created from one unit of reserves in the banking system.

Velocity of Money Velocity of Money

Shows how many units of goods or services one unit of money enables to change hands. It is expressed as GNP / Money Stock.

quantity theory of money quantity theory of money

The body of principles maintaining that there is a same-directional and proportional relationship between the money supply and the general price level.

neutrality of money neutrality of money

The view maintaining that the money supply in the economy determines only the nominal magnitudes and will not affect the real values.

Monetary Transmission Mechanism Monetary Transmission Mechanism

Shows through which channels and to what extent monetary variables affect aggregate demand, the output gap and inflation. The monetary transmission mechanism is generally explained in three stages. The first stage determines the transmission of the changes in monetary policy implementations to variables such as interest rates, asset prices, expectations and the exchange rate. In the second stage, the said variables affect the demand for domestic and imported goods; in the third stage, aggregate demand and domestic pricing behaviors are determined, and domestic prices and import prices shape inflation. In addition, interest rates have direct effects on inflation, and exchange rates on the demand for imported goods and on import prices in local currency.

Monetary Gold Monetary Gold

Refers to the gold belonging to the central bank and held as reserves.

Monetary Aggregates Monetary Aggregates

A monetary magnitude is calculated by subtracting the monetary sector's liabilities to one another from the total of the money in circulation and the various liabilities of the monetary sector (the central bank, banks and money market funds) that are monetary or convertible into money. There are various monetary magnitude definitions according to the degree of liquidity of the assets they contain: M1: consists of the total of the money in circulation and demand deposits. M2: consists of the total of M1 and time deposits. M3: M3, the most broadly defined money supply, consists of the total of M2, the funds provided from repos, money market funds and issued securities (with maturities of up to two years).

monetary growth rate rule monetary growth rate rule

The monetary policy principle proposing that the central bank increase the money supply in proportion to the growth rate of real GDP.

money income money income

The income consisting only of payments in the form of money.

monetary targeting monetary targeting

The monetary policy regime in which the central bank targets a certain rate of increase for monetary magnitudes such as the money supply and bank reserves.

Monetary Sector Monetary Sector

It can also be defined as the money-creating sector. It covers the central bank, deposit banks, development and investment banks, participation banks and money market funds.

monetarist economic theory monetarist economic theory

The school of thought maintaining that the changes seen in real income in the short run stem from demand shocks related to the money supply, and advocating the state's intervention in the economy through rule-based monetary policy.

Pareto efficiency Pareto efficiency

The allocation of resources in which, while improving the situation of some individuals, no other individual's situation is worsened.

Parity Parity

The value of one country's currency calculated against the currency of a reference country, with that country's currency taken as the basis.

Passive job search passive job search

The state of waiting for responses to the applications previously made to the active job-search channels.

Undertakings coming together for a project gather the patents they hold in a pool and open them to the use of the other undertakings in the project. Stakeholder

All the social parties with which the enterprise interacts, that are affected by the enterprise's activities, and that affect the enterprise through their activities.

Market market

The physical or virtual environment where buyers and sellers come together, and in this process the prices of products are determined.

Per Se

In competition law, per se rules have been adopted to deem unlawful, in almost all cases, those behaviors whose natural and inevitable effects are clearly anticompetitive and for which a detailed study is not needed to show that they are unlawful. These are the practical rules of the US judicial process. Per se rules are accepted in cases where experience shows that certain behaviors will cause serious anticompetitive outcomes and can hardly ever be justified. Accordingly,

Perfect Competition

A hypothetical market model in which, owing to the presence of a great many buyers and sellers, it is not possible for individuals to influence prices, so prices are taken as given; entries into and exits from the market are entirely free; there is the opportunity of full information about market conditions; goods are homogeneous; the rational behavior pattern directed toward profit maximization is dominant; and production and exchange can be carried out free of any limitation. It is known that such a market cannot exist in reality

Performance Indicator

The scales producing quantitative information about projects and enabling the project targets to be defined in a clear and measurable way.

Persons

The administrative fines of up to five percent of the fine imposed on the undertaking or undertaking association, given to the managers or employees of the undertaking or undertaking association whose determining influence in the infringement is established, regulated in Article 16(4) of the Competition Act in the event that fines relating to the substance are imposed on undertakings or undertaking associations.

Phillips curve Phillips curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the unemployment and inflation rates, all else being constant.

The analysis put forward by the British economist Arthur Cecil Pigou, stating that when the general price level decreases, aggregate demand will increase owing to the appreciation of wealth.

Or in short S: the quantity of a product that all the sellers in the market want to sell, depending on different prices, in a given period.

market equilibrium market equilibrium

market disequilibrium market disequilibrium

market-clearing price market-clearing price

Market or marketplace market

The physical or virtual environment where buyers and sellers come together, and in this process the prices of products are determined.

Market Maker System Primary Dealership

A system in which, with the aim of increasing effectiveness in primary market transactions and facilitating the functioning of secondary markets, the treasury or central banks accept as counterparty only the banks and certain other institutions it selects according to certain criteria, in transactions such as debt security issuance (auction) and foreign exchange intervention. The institutions selected under the name of market maker have obligations such as transacting uninterruptedly in the secondary markets, giving quotations, and purchasing a certain amount of an issue.

Market structure market structure

Platform Economies

Platform economies are the formations enabling two (or more) different but interlinked user groups operating in a two (or multi)-sided market to interact in a way that creates value for at least one of the sides. Their most frequently observed examples are online demand-coordinating platforms (online marketplaces, general or specialized search sites) and hardware/software platforms.

Policy ineffectiveness proposition policy ineffectiveness proposition

Policy interest rate policy interest rate

policy mix policy mix

Portfolio portfolio

Position

The strengthening by an undertaking holding a dominant position in a market of its dominant position, particularly by increasing market share, at the end of a concentration transaction.

Potential GDP potential GDP

; It is the level of real GDP that is sustainable depending on natural, demographic, technological or institutional constraints.

Among the persons of working age who are neither employed nor unemployed: those who are seeking work but are not in a state to start work within a short time, and those who, without seeking work, have a desire to work and are in a state to be able to start work within a short time.

Potential Competitor

In the event of a small and permanent increase in prices, the undertaking having the possibility (and desire) of entering the market, bearing the necessary conversion costs or making the mandatory investments, is accepted as a potential rival.

Position Excess Long Position

Refers to the net surplus position held in foreign currency, securities or any financial instrument. For example, having a 10 million US dollar cash surplus position means having, net (after cash US dollar debts are deducted), 10 million US dollars in cash in a portfolio. In other words, it expresses a surplus holding in an instrument.

Positive externality positive externality

The beneficial effect an economic activity has on persons who are not party to that activity.

Positive analysis positive analysis

The analytical approach treating economic behavior and systems with an objective perspective, trying only to describe them without judging.

Positive output gap positive output gap

Or an expansionary gap: the situation in which, in the short run, real GDP is above potential GDP, and hence the economy is considered to be in an expansion period.

Price Leadership

Refers to the situation in which an undertaking in a dominant position, or whose leadership is accepted by the others, changes its prices and the other undertakings in the market adopt and follow this price. Apart from the price leader's being in a dominant position, on what criteria it is determined/selected is a matter that varies from market to market and requires research. Nevertheless, when price leadership is adopted to facilitate tacit agreement, the price leader generally has a high

Price Recommendation

Suppliers' recommending the price at which a good will be resold is evaluated, within the scope of competition law, according to whether this recommendation turns into fixed or minimum price setting. The recommended price practice has two drawbacks from the standpoint of competition law.

Price Rigidity

Price rigidity refers to the price of a good, service or production factor remaining constant despite perceptible changes in supply and demand conditions, or changing in only one direction. Price rigidity, also called price stickiness, is a matter closely concerning competition policies. For price rigidity is a phenomenon that can stem from a lack of competition and negatively affect social welfare. Market structure and undertakings' behaviors can create price rigidity. In general

Primary Market

Special terms are used to refer to the markets where the sale of the main product and the side products that need to be purchased along with it or later than it is realized. The first product the customer buys is called the primary product, and the product needed later for that product to be usable the secondary product. The markets where the trade of the primary and secondary products takes place are, respectively, the primary/fore market and the secondary/aftermarket

Producer Surplus

The difference between the price the producer actually sells at and the price it is willing to sell at is called the producer surplus. The concept of producer surplus is dealt with within the scope of competition economics/policy because, when there is a price increase in the market, while the consumer surplus decreases, this decrease is not transferred as an equal amount of producer surplus (and the deadweight loss thereby formed) results in a fall in total social welfare.

Production Joint Ventures

The joint ventures formed with the aim of producing. Production joint ventures can be fully functional, or can also emerge as non-fully functional (partially functional) joint ventures undertaking only a limited part of the parent undertakings' fields of activity. The reason for partial functionality is generally that, because these ventures make use of the parent undertakings' raw material sources and technical knowledge, they cannot behave independently in the markets, and the sale of the produced products is left to the parent undertakings

Profit

In economic theory and in the accounting discipline it is possible to speak of two separate profit concepts that differ from one another. The profit concept used in accounting expresses the revenue surplus remaining in the firm's hands after it has covered the costs of all the inputs it used in production. Profit in the economic sense, on the other hand, expresses the revenue surplus formed after the opportunity cost of producing the good is also added to the total costs. In this case, a firm earning zero profit in the economic sense still earns normal

Profit Maximization

One of the fundamental assumptions on which microeconomic theory rests is that firms realize their production quantities at the level that maximizes their profits. At this production quantity, the price level forming in the market is named 'the price at the level where profit is maximized'. In microeconomic theory this point is the price formed according to the demand function at the production level where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

Program

On the other hand, with the aim of protecting the confidentiality of trade secrets, Article 239 of the Turkish Penal Code No. 5237 regulates the offense of disclosing trade secrets, banking secrets or customer secrets

Public Good/Service

“ They are goods and services that do not have "competition in consumption" and "exclusion" characteristics. If one person's consumption of a good does not reduce others' consumption of that good, it is considered that the good does not have the characteristic of "competition in consumption". If one person's consumption of a good does not exclude others from consuming that good, it is considered that the good does not have the characteristic of "exclusion". Such goods/services can be provided by the state as well as by private enterprises.

Ramsey Pricing

Ramsey pricing envisages that prices be set inversely proportional to demand elasticity, so that welfare losses can be brought down to the lowest level. In the case where there are demands of different elasticity (sensitivity) for the same product, on the other hand, Ramsey pricing envisages that this product be offered to different consumer groups at different prices according to consumers' sensitivity to price. While a low price is applied to the consumer group whose demand is elastic (price-sensitive), to the consumer group whose demand is inelastic

Rastsal olay random event

A set of outcomes each of which has a certain probability of realization.

Rayiç Bedel

Re-export

The sale of purchased foreign-origin or Turkish-origin goods that have been sold abroad, to another country, in transit or directly, without being subject to the provisions of the import and export regimes, whether or not a transfer is made for the value of the goods.

Rebate Schemes/Systems

Rebate systems can emerge in very different forms under the dynamic conditions of commercial life, and vary in their structures, workings and effects. If the earning of the rebate in any rebate system is made conditional on the purchase of a single product, such rebates are accepted as 'single-product rebates'. However, if the purchase condition in the rebate system covers multiple products or markets, the said rebates are 'bundle rebates'

Reciprocity Agreement

A type of bilateral (or multilateral) agreement made among undertakings in order to provide one another favorable conditions, or to buy from and sell to one another mutually. In reciprocity agreements, an undertaking can be obliged to purchase from the undertaking that purchases from it. Thanks to this agreement, the undertaking can obtain a price reduction by making its purchases from its own customers, or can activate its idle capacity. These competitive effects that reciprocity agreements can create

Reel döviz kuru real exchange rate

Or in short RER: the exchange rate calculated by taking into account the difference in the general price levels between two countries.

Reel efektif döviz kuru real effective exchange rate

The effective exchange rate calculated by taking into account the inter-country relative price changes.

Reel faiz Real interest rate

Interest stripped of inflation; by the Fisher equation (1+real) = (1+nominal)/(1+inflation), approximately real ≈ nominal − inflation.

Reel Faiz Oranı Real Interest Rate

The nominal interest rate stripped of inflation. Technically, it is found by subtracting the expected inflation rate from the nominal interest rate.

Reel GSYH real GDP

Or GDP in fixed prices: the national income method measuring the value of the goods and services produced in a given period at the prices of a fixed base year.

Real business cycle theory Real business cycle theory

The school of thought maintaining that the changes seen in real income in the short run stem from supply shocks, and advocating the state's intervention in the economy through supply-side policies.

Real Exports Real Exports

It is expressed with the export quantity index. The export quantity index measures the change occurring in the export quantity, on the condition that prices are fixed. Export quantity indices are calculated by TUIK.

Real Imports Real Imports

It is expressed with the import quantity index. The import quantity index measures the change occurring in the import quantity, on the condition that prices are fixed. Import quantity indices are calculated by TUIK.

Real Sector Confidence Index - RSCI Real Sector Confidence Index - RSCI

An indicator in which the answers given to the different questions of the Business Tendency Survey are evaluated together and summarized, with the aim of bringing out the general impressions of real sector representatives about the economic outlook. To access the Real Sector Confidence Index

Rediscount Rediscount

Refers to the rediscounting — the exchanging for a consideration again (rediscount) — of the instruments that have already been discounted, in other words exchanged for a consideration (discount). It is an instrument used by central banks in monetary policy implementations, under the name rediscount window, by subjecting various bills to discounting (re-discount), on the condition that they determine their own conditions.

Rediscount credit discount credit

Rediscount rate discount rate

The interest rate the central bank applies for its rediscount credits.

Rejection of the Transactions

The non-implementation by the relevant financial institutions of the transactions sought to be carried out at the financial institutions. These are the transactions in which the financial institutions could not carry out the identification and verification of the identity of the customer or of the person finally benefiting from the transaction, could not determine to whom the ownership and control belong in legal persons and partnerships, and could not have information about the type and purpose of the transaction being carried out

Reliance on Intermediaries and

Third Parties: The leaving, under certain conditions, by the financial institutions of the fulfillment of the measures relating to the identification and verification of the customer's and the beneficiary's identity, the determination of to whom the ownership and control belong in legal persons and partnerships, and the obtaining of information about the type and purpose of the transaction sought to be carried out, in the customer due diligence process, to intermediary institutions or other third parties. In this case, all the responsibility relating to the identification and verification of the customer's identity falls on the third party

Repo Repurchase Agreement

It is generally used in cases where the liquidity tightness in the market is temporary, with the aim of increasing the banking system's liquidity for a temporary period. The central bank buys instruments with a commitment to resell them at a future date (at the price determined during the transaction) from the institutions authorized to conduct open market operations. The resale price is determined on the date the purchase transaction is made. The institution party to the transaction also undertakes to buy the instrument subject to the repo transaction at the transaction's maturity. From the central bank's perspective, the repo transaction expresses the temporary provision of liquidity to the market within the framework of open market operations, for the duration of the transaction's maturity, in return for the instruments subject to the repo.

Example: Securities sold under a repurchase agreement have been recorded as collateralized borrowing.( The securities sold under the repurchase agreement were recorded as a collateralised borrowing.

English definition: An agreement to sell securities with a commitment to buy them back at a later date.

Reserves

According to the principle contributed to the industrial economics literature by E.A.G. Robinson for the first time in 1958, as the scale of a production unit increases, savings can be achieved in the proportion of the reserve capacity set aside to meet future demand. For example, the number of beds a large hospital leaves empty for sudden needs will be less than the number of beds left empty by two small hospitals half its size.

Recession Recession

The being of economic growth negative or slow for a certain period. It can also be defined as the presence of idle capacity in the economy, or the economy's growing at a rate lower than its long-run growth rate.

Restriction of Technology

The designing by the undertaking of the new technology, although it is possible to design it in another way, in a way that other undertakings cannot use, in order to give itself an advantage — in other words, creating a barrier to market entry. This situation can be unlawful if carried out by the undertaking holding a dominant position and the other conditions are also present.

Restrictions on Resale Price

In a vertical relationship, the setting by the seller of the buyer's fixed or minimum resale price is prohibited under Article 4 of the Competition Act. However, on the condition that it does not turn into fixed or minimum resale prices, it is possible for the supplier to determine the buyer's maximum resale price or to recommend a resale price to the buyer. So that the maximum or recommended resale prices notified to the buyer do not turn into minimum or fixed prices, it is necessary that the said prices be published as maximum or recommended in the published price lists

Revaluation Revaluation

Refers to the increase in the value of the national currency against foreign currencies. For example, the rise of the value of the Turkish lira against the US dollar from 1.3 TL to 1.2 TL (the US dollar losing value) means that the TL has gained 0.1 TL in value.

Example: The revaluation of the property increased its carrying amount and recognised the surplus in other comprehensive income.( A revaluation of the property increased its carrying amount and recognised the surplus in other comprehensive income.

English definition: The remeasurement of a non-current asset to its fair value, with the increase recognised in other comprehensive income.

Reserve reserve

The total of the cash in banks' vaults and their accounts at the central bank.

Example: The revaluation reserve is presented within equity.( The revaluation reserve is presented within equity.

English definition: A component of equity set aside for a purpose.

Reserve Option Coefficient - ROK Reserve Option Coefficient - ROC

The coefficients determining the foreign currency or gold counterpart that can be established per unit of Turkish lira reserve requirement in the Reserve Option Mechanism.

Reserve Option Mechanism - ROM Reserve Option Mechanism - ROM

A practice permitting banks and other financial institutions to establish a certain percentage of their Turkish lira reserve requirements in foreign currency and gold.

Rezerv Opsiyonu Oranı Reserve Option Ratio

The ratio showing what percentage of banks' Turkish lira reserve requirements can be established in foreign currency or gold in the Reserve Option Mechanism.

Rezerv Para Hard Currency

Refers to the assets in foreign currency and gold held in the portfolios of central banks and international financial institutions. Accordingly, for a payment instrument to carry the property of reserve currency, its value against other currencies must be stable, it must belong to a country with a large share in world trade, and it must be readily bought and sold in the foreign exchange markets.

Rezerv para birimi reserve currency

The currency held as official reserves at central banks because it is widely used in international transactions.

Rezerv varlıklar reserve assets

The main heading in the balance of payments showing the central bank's official foreign exchange reserves.

Rights of Complainant

The rights the complainant has within the framework of the legislation, such as the right to lodge a complaint, the right to resort to the judiciary against the Board's decisions, the right to receive the reasoned decision, the right to be informed, the right to request that its name remain confidential, and the right to attend the oral defense hearing.

Risk risk

The degree to which the outcome realized regarding a future event can differ from the expected outcome.

Example: The entity discloses the nature and extent of the risks arising from financial instruments.( The entity discloses the nature and extent of the risks arising from financial instruments.

English definition: The possibility that actual outcomes will differ from expected outcomes, including financial risks such as credit, liquidity and market risk.

Risk havuzu Risk pool

The risk-distribution method in which several insurance companies come together and share a certain risk.

Risk İştahı Risk Appetite

The desire to buy, which increases together with the growth of positive expectations in the financial markets and decreases with negative expectations.

Risk Primi Risk Premium

Refers to the additional return that a risky asset or instrument provides to the investor relative to an entirely riskless asset or instrument. The risk premium of an asset or instrument can also be counted as an indicator of the compensation obtained relative to the entirely riskless investment instrument.

Risk seven risk lover

The person who, between two options with the same expected value, prefers the riskier one.

Risk-Getiri Risk-Return

Refers to the relationship between the return expected to be obtained from an investment made in any asset or instrument and the risk assumed with the investment made in the said asset or instrument. In principle, there is a positive relationship between the risk assumed and the expected return. Hence, particularly in the financial markets, as the risk assumed increases, the return is expected to increase, and as the risk assumed decreases, the return is expected to decrease. Risk is generally expressed by the standard deviation of the investment's past returns (historical volatility). The expected return from the investment, on the other hand, is the average of the past returns. The risk-return curve formed by the maximum returns that can be obtained in return for a certain risk is called the 'efficient frontier', and its use is particularly for comparison and benchmark purposes.

Riske Maruz Değer Value at Risk - VaR

The statistical method used to measure the riskiness of the financial assets in a company or an investment portfolio. The method points to the highest loss level that can occur in the value of a portfolio, within a certain confidence interval, over a predetermined period. Risk managers aim, with the VaR method, to measure and control the risk assumed.

Example: Value at risk estimates potential losses over a specific period.( Value-at-risk estimates losses over a given period.)

İngilizce tanım: A statistical measure of potential loss.

Riske tarafsız risk neutral

The person who is indifferent between two options with the same expected value.

Riskte maruz değer Value at Risk - VaR

Shows the greatest loss the portfolio value can suffer at a certain confidence level and maturity; VaR = z·σ·Portfolio value. For multi-day horizons the scaling factor is the square root of days (10 days = √10 times, NOT 10 times).

Riskten kaçınan risk averse

The person who, between two options with the same expected value, prefers the less risky one.

Risk Averse, Risk Lover, Risk Neutral Risk Neutral

The concepts used to express an investor's preferences in the face of risk. While a risk-averse investor settles for a low but predictable return instead of an uncertain high return in the future, a risk-loving investor tends to take high risk even though the expected returns are equal. In contrast, a risk-neutral investor is the investor who makes no choice between risk and return.

Riskten Korunma Hedging

The securing of the investor's investment against possible adverse price movements, by using the instruments in the financial markets effectively and correctly, with the aim of protection against investment risk. With the aim of reducing the risks that may be encountered to a certain value, the investor can, by taking a long position with the help of futures contracts, purchase a futures contract with the expectation that prices will rise in the future, or, by taking a short position, sell a futures contract with the expectation that prices will fall in the future.

Example: The company applied hedge accounting to its interest rate swaps.( The company applied hedge accounting to its interest rate swaps.

English definition: Designating a derivative to offset changes in fair value or cash flows.

License

The document given by the municipalities, provincial special administrations, organized industrial zones or the Ministry of Industry and Technology, as a result of the conditions sought in the workplaces specified in the regulation according to the activity being met. Redemption: the transaction of eliminating the debt by the debtor through payments made at once or in certain periods. Import Substitution: the domestic production of products previously imported.

constant cost industry constant cost industry

fixed input fixed input

fixed capital fixed capital

consumption on fixed capital consumption on fixed capital

pure oligopoly pure oligoply
