Custodian Service Custodian Service

The services relating to the capital market instruments deposited or delivered, by book entry or physically, in connection with capital market activities — whether by reason of capital market activities, or in the capacity of custodian, or for administration, or as collateral, or under whatever name — to the capital market instruments.

Samurai Bonds

The securities issues made in Japan, in Japanese yen, by foreigners. They are mostly issues with maturities of 5 years and over. The first issue was made in 1970 by the Asian Development Bank.

Industrial clustering industrial clustering

The more effective working of interrelated firms using similar infrastructure and production factors by gathering in a certain geographical region.

Chamber of Industry

The professional organizations possessing legal personality and of the nature of public institutions, established by law with the aim of ensuring solidarity among industrialists, working for the solution of their common problems, and protecting their common interests.

Chamber of Industry

A document given to the industrial enterprises evaluated within the scope of Article 1 of the Industrial Registry Law No. 6948, and to the enterprises making continuous and serial repairs and the large construction sites such as power plants producing electricity or other energy and shipbuilding, which must be obtained within 2 (two) months from the date on which the enterprise began its production activity. The said document is drawn up by the Provincial Directorates of Industry and Technology.

Industrial Production Index - IPI Industry Production Index - IPI

An index calculated monthly in order to measure the short-term positive or negative effects of the developments occurring in the economy and of the economic policies implemented. According to the NACE Rev.2 classification, it covers the sectors of mining and quarrying, manufacturing, and the production and distribution of electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning.

Put Option Put Option

It expresses the right to sell. It gives the party holding the option contract the right to sell the instrument underlying the option under the conditions stated in the option, but brings no obligation. Depending on market conditions, the party holding the option may not exercise the option. The exercise of the option is expressed as being 'exercised'. The party selling the option, on the other hand, is obliged to fulfill the terms of the contract if the buying party wants to exercise the option.

Example: The non-controlling interest held a put option that could require the group to buy its shares.( The non-controlling interest held a put option that could require the group to buy its shares.

English definition: A contract giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to sell an asset at a set price.

Purchasing Power Parity Purchasing Power Parity

The exchange rate that equalizes the prices of similar goods and services subject to trade in a certain basket across different countries. Since, in calculating purchasing power parity, only the goods and services subject to trade are taken into consideration, such a calculation can fall short of measuring the true value of the rate of exchange between the two countries' currencies.

Purchasing Managers Index Purchasing Managers Index - PMI

A diffusion index obtained from the answers the purchasing managers of industrial firms give to questions about the development of production, orders, employment, suppliers' delivery times and input stocks.

Sale Ask, Offer

The price at which the market participants are willing to sell the values traded in the market (such as foreign currency and securities).

Example: Revenue from sales is accounted for when control is transferred.( Revenue from the sale is recognised when control transfers.

English definition: Transferring an asset in exchange for consideration.

Search Warrant Authorization

( A permit issued by a judicial authority (judge) for law enforcement to conduct a search. SECI (Southeast European Cooperation Initiative) is the Southeast European Cooperation Initiative established pursuant to the "Agreement on Cooperation and Combat Transborder Crime" signed in Bucharest on May 26, 1999. The purpose of the initiative is to assist each other in the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of transborder crimes among the participating countries. Its center is in Bucharest.

Second Best

The level closest to the conditions of full competition. One of the most important justifications of competition policies is the thought that the fully competitive market leads societies to the highest welfare level, the 'first best'. However, it is known that full competition is a utopian model and that, in practice, it will not be possible to satisfy the conditions of full competition. For this reason, the aim of competition policies is to minimize the departures from the rules of full competition so that social welfare rises to the highest possible level — that is, the 'second best'

Sectoral Foreign Trade Company

The companies established in order to enable the enterprises in the same production field to open up to their foreign markets by uniting under an organization for the purpose of exporting.

Selective Pricing

The selective low pricing, independent of costs, among customers or products, undertaken by the undertakings in a dominant position with the aim of making their rivals' activities difficult.

Senyoraj - Beylik Hakkı Seigniorage

The real revenue the institution holding the authority to print money obtains by printing money by virtue of this authority. It is expressed as the ratio of the change in the money stock to the general price level. In the case where inflation stems only from the increase in the quantity of money, seigniorage and the inflation tax equal one another.

Serbest Dalgalı Kur Rejimi Free-Floating Exchange Rate Regime

Refers to the system in which the exchange rate is determined according to the supply and demand conditions in the market. Central banks never intervene in the market, or very rarely, only in extraordinary conditions.

Serbest nakit akışı Free Cash Flow - FCF

The portion of cash generated from operating activities that remains after capital expenditures are deducted; it is an input to DCF valuation.

Serbest piyasa ekonomisi free market economy

The economic system in a country in which decisions on what to produce, how, and for whom are taken as a result of the interaction of buyers and sellers in the markets.

Serbest rezerv excess reserve

The reserves a bank holds in addition to its required reserve amount.

Serbest Yatırım Fonu Hedge Fon

Refers to a type of investment fund whose certain restrictions have been minimized and in which as flexible an investment strategy as possible can be followed. The fundamental difference of hedge funds from ordinary investment funds is the possibilities of short selling and of borrowing (being able to invest with borrowed resources). Furthermore, thanks to hedge funds, the investor can take short and long positions, apply arbitrage strategies, at the same time both buy and sell a security priced below its value, invest in options or bonds, and invest in any kind of market carrying the possibility of obtaining high returns under low risk.

Sermaye arzı supply of capital

Or in short SK: the total quantity of capital that all the units in the economy want to rent out, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.

Sermaye Hesabı Capital Account

It contains the flows arising through the acquisition and disposal of non-produced, non-financial assets (intangible assets such as a piece of land, and intangible assets such as franchises, trademarks and leases — transferable contracts) and capital transfers (such as debt forgiveness and other capital transfers).

Sermaye kaçışı capital flight

The international capital flows taking place outside the knowledge and supervision of the state.

Sermaye Koruma Tamponu Capital Conservation Buffer

Refers to the additional core capital amount that banks are expected to hold, with the aim of preventing equity from falling short of the regulations on capital adequacy owing to the losses that may be encountered in the event of the deterioration of the economic and financial indicators.

Sermaye Piyasası Capital Market

The markets in which investment instruments with maturities longer than one year are issued and traded.

Sermaye piyasası dengesi capital market equilibrium

The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of capital demanded in the market equals the quantity of capital supplied.

Sermaye talebi demand for capital

Or in short DK: the total quantity of capital that all the units in the economy want to rent, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.

Sermayenin kira oranı rental rate of capital

Or in short PK: the payment made for using one unit of capital in production.

Sermayenin marjinal ürün geliri marginal revenue product of capital

Or in short MRPK: the change seen in total revenue when the quantity of capital is increased by one unit.

Sermayenin marjinal ürünü marginal product of capital

Or in short MPK: the change seen in the total quantity of product when the quantity of capital is increased by one unit.

Sermayenin ortalama ürünü average product of capital

Or in short APK: the quantity of product produced per unit of capital in a given period.

Sharing Economy

The sharing economy is an economic system based on the foundation of a good or service being shared by its owner, for a fee or free of charge, over an online platform. The sharing economy refers to the renting or sharing of goods rather than their purchase. In the sharing economy, the owner of a good, such as a house, a car or a bicycle, rents out a good it is not using to another person for a temporary period. The online platforms on which the sharing transaction is carried out depend on people being able to trust one another

Sharpe oranı Sharpe ratio

The ratio of the portfolio's excess return to its standard deviation: (Rp − Rf) / σp. It measures the premium per unit of total risk; beta is not used.

Sigorta insurance

The service of providing financial protection against various risks.

Sigorta piyasası insurance market

The physical or virtual environment where insurance policies are bought and sold, and in this process the insurance premium rates are determined.

Sigorta poliçesi insurance policy

The contract giving the assurance of a certain payment in the event of the realization of predetermined damages and losses.

Sigorta primi insurance premium

The payment made in return for the insurance policy.

Single Unit Discounts

If the rebate systems applied by undertakings are made conditional on the buyer's fulfilling the purchase condition relating to a single product/market, such rebates are called 'single-product rebates'. For example, a tire shop's earning a premium in return for making a certain amount of sales annually is a kind of single-product rebate.

Sistem riski systemic risk

The risk of payment disruptions arising across the financial system because of adverse economic developments.

Systematic risk Systematic risk

The risk affecting the market as a whole and not eliminable by diversification (interest, inflation and exchange rate shocks); beta measures this risk.

Systemic Risk Systemic Risk

The interruption of financial services, in a part of or the whole financial system, in a way that can also lead to serious adverse consequences on economic activity, is called systemic risk. Whether any financial institution's financial insufficiency is a source of systemic risk depends on the effect stemming from this insufficiency being able to spread to the whole of the financial system and hence to the economy in general.

Lender of last resort Lender of last resort

The institution that is willing to lend even when no one else is.

Result

The measurable, concrete situations expected to form within 1-3 years following the completion of the project, obtained in line with the specific aims determined at the outset. Social Enterprise: the type of venture that aims to make profit but uses the profit it obtains to produce benefit for society. Social Innovation: the term for the innovative works used in addressing the problems and needs arising in societies.

Example: The result for the year was reported after tax.( The result for the year was reported after tax.

English definition: The profit or loss for a period.

Social security contributions Social security contributions

The portion of labor income paid to the social security institutions.

Social Security Institutions Budget Social Security Institutions Budget

The budget of the public administrations providing social security services, such as the Social Security Institution and the Turkish Employment Agency.

Social Capital

The concept expressing the values in social life of the bonds, union, togetherness, solidarity, mutual assistance, love, respect, trust and morality among individuals.

Special and Exclusive Rights

Special rights are the rights given by the state, through any legal, regulatory or administrative way, to a limited number of undertakings, to be within a certain geographical area. An exclusive right, on the other hand, is the right arising from the state's establishing a monopoly, through any legal instrument, in favor of a single undertaking (public or private) for the conduct of a certain economic activity in a certain geographical area for a certain period.

Speculative motive Speculative motive

The demand for money stemming from the thought of making gains from the expected future price changes of financial or non-financial assets.

Spot Market Spot Market

The market in which the purchase or sale of a product is realized, at the price determined on the transaction date, at the latest within two business days thereafter.

Spot Valör Spot Date

The realization, within two business days following the day on which the transaction is made, of the payments connected with a transaction carried out in the financial markets. If a transaction made with spot value date, for example, took place on Monday, the payments are made on Wednesday. In other words, the spot value date expresses the date on which the money will be ready for use. The difference between the transaction date and the date of use stems from operations such as the preparation of messages, the making of controls and the provision of funds requiring a certain time.

Stackelberg modeli Stackelberg model

A duopoly model in which one of the two identical firms producing a homogeneous product makes its output choice being aware of the mutual interdependence, while the other is unaware of it.

Stagflasyon Stagflation

Refers to the situation that occurs when inflation rises in an environment in which production in an economy has fallen or at least has not increased.

Standart sapma Standard deviation

The square-rooted measure of the deviation of the returns from their average; it is the standard gauge of total risk (volatility) in finance.

Standart Vadeli İşlemler Futures

It means forward transactions. It envisages the delivery of a certain instrument, at a previously determined price, again on a previously determined date. Its difference from forward markets is that it trades over contracts standardized in organized markets (such as the quantity of a contract, the market release dates of the contracts, and having a collateral system under the name of margin). When done for speculative purposes, theoretically there is the possibility of infinite profit and loss.

Standart Vadeli İşlemler Sözleşmesi Futures Contracts

The contract giving the parties to the contract the obligation to buy or sell, at the agreed price, a good or instrument of standardized quality and quantity, on a determined future date.

Start-Up Costs

The establishment costs incurred for the building, vehicles, machinery, equipment, legal expenses, advertising, worker training, etc. necessary to begin an activity. Particularly in cases where these costs carry the nature of sunk costs, entry into the market becomes significantly more difficult.

Statute of Limitations

The periods regulated in Articles 20 and 21 of the Misdemeanors Law No. 5326, which prevent the Competition Board from deciding on an administrative fine (the limitation of the investigation) or the implementation of this decision (the limitation of implementation).

Sterilizasyon Sterilization

The open market operations central banks make in order to balance the effects of the increases in the money supply arising for various reasons. For example, when the central bank buys foreign currency, it tries to withdraw the increase in the money supply from the market through the sale of securities, thereby sterilizing the intervention made in the foreign exchange market.

Stok stock

The ready productions awaiting sale in order to generate income in the future.

Strategic Behaviour

Acting strategically, taking into account also the behaviors of the other persons who can affect the decision. Instead of the assumption in classical economics that each person will take their decisions independently of the others' reactions, it is thought within the framework of game theory that persons will decide taking also the others' reactions into account.

Strategic Cooperation

( "Strategic Alliance) Agreements between two or more enterprises that, while maintaining their autonomy, jointly carry out specific activities such as technology, expertise, and production in which they have competitive advantages, or that aim to achieve common competitive goals, which are contract-based agreements that do not require the establishment of a new legal entity (transfer of control) and are located between simple commercial contracts and merger transactions, are short-term, flexible structured"

"Strategy" "strategy"

The term for the choices economic units make in order to reach their aims.

"Strategic Investment"

The investments of strategic importance, having the potential to raise our international competitiveness, directed toward the production of products with high import dependence, with the aim of reducing the current account deficit.

"Strategic Product"

The term for the intermediate goods with a high import ratio, whose domestic production is encouraged through various support mechanisms, with the aim of reducing the current account deficit.

"Structure - Conduct-Performance Paradigm"

According to this approach, developed in the 1940s and playing a determining role in the American industrial economics literature between 1940 and 1970, an industry's performance depends, depending on the structure of the market, on the behaviors of the buyers and sellers in the market; the market structure in turn depends on fundamental conditions such as technology and demand. Hence structure is used as the predictor of conduct and performance. The market's structure (such as full competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly) is generally defined with concentration rates

"Subprime Markets" "Subprime Markets"

The markets where persons with a poor credit history can obtain credit at a higher interest. If this credit has been taken for the purpose of buying a home, it is called 'subprime mortgage'. The institutions extending the credit can re-release these credits to the market by dividing them into risk groups and can seek investors who will purchase them.

"Subsidiary"

The concept of an affiliated company refers to the company of which an undertaking has, directly or indirectly, more than half of its capital or its commercial assets, the authority to exercise more than half of the voting rights, the authority to appoint more than half of the members of the audit board, the board of directors or the organs legally authorized to represent the business, or the right to manage its business.

"Substitutability"

Substitutability refers to the ability of goods or services to be used in place of another good or service in production or consumption. Substitutability results in producers/consumers moving between the two products when the demands of the two products interact with one another and it is profitable. Substitute goods have a positive cross-price elasticity of demand. From the standpoint of competition law, whether the two products take place in the same market is determined according to the degree of substitution between the products

"Sukuk"

The Islamic financing certificate issued for asset financing, based on the principle that the income to be obtained from the asset or investment purchased with the fund obtained through its issuance is paid to the sukuk holders at certain periods. In its simplest form, sukuk shows the ownership of an asset or the right to benefit from it. The right and claim contained in the sukuk is not only the right to a cash flow, but also the right of ownership. This differentiates the sukuk from conventional bonds. While conventional bonds consist of interest-bearing securities, the sukuk is fundamentally a security consisting of the right of ownership in an asset basket. The bond can be characterized as a debt-based certificate, and the sukuk as an asset-based certificate.

"Super Dominance"

The concept of super-dominance is used to express the market power approaching monopoly, as a result of the market power's persisting for a long time. It corresponds to the power held by monopolies or near-monopoly undertakings, and approximately over 90% market share is associated with this concept.

"Sweezy model" "Sweezy model"

Or the kinked demand curve model: the oligopoly model in which the demand for a firm's good depends on the response of the rival firms to a price change.

"Switching Cost"

Every kind of cost the customer encounters, outside the price of the good or service, at the stage of switching to a new provider. For example, in cases where number portability among operators is not possible, the customer's changing their GSM operator creates the cost of informing the persons in the phone book about the number change. The transaction cost of changing provider, the capacity to learn to use the new product, the necessity of the new product being compatible with the existing equipment, the untried brands

"SWOT Analysis"

An analysis method, carried out concerning the current situation, based on the determination of the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. It is formed from the initial letters of the English words strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. Completion Visa: the approval given that an investment made by obtaining an Investment Incentive Certificate has been completed.

"Contract"

The contract arranged between the investor and the OSB relating to the allocation of the parcel, following the delivery by the real or legal persons found suitable for parcel allocation in the Organized Industrial Zones of the Investment Commitment, notarized, to the OSB.

"Subsidy" "subsidy"

The unconditional payment or tax reduction made by the state, taking the public interest into account.

"Sustainable growth" sustainable growth

The long-run economic growth that can realistically be achieved within the framework of an action plan taking into account the limited natural resources and the environmental effects.

Sustainability

The method of being able to meet today's economic and social needs without restricting the possibilities of future generations and without harming nature.

Continuous income permanent income

In contrast to the income obtained in the current period, the expectation of the average income that economic units think they will earn over their lifetime.

Permanent Income Hypothesis Permanent Income Hypothesis

The view maintaining that economic units determine their consumption not according to their income in the current period, but according to the average income they expect to earn over their lifetime.

Frictional unemployment frictional unemployment

Or voluntary unemployment: the type of unemployment stemming from individuals' entering and leaving the labor market and their temporary waits between jobs.

Herd behavior Herding behavior

Transacting by following the direction of the crowd instead of the individual decision; it feeds the inflation of bubbles and their collapse in panic.

Sürünen kur crawling peg

The fixed exchange rate regime in which the nominal exchange rates are regularly adjusted according to selected economic indicators.

Sıfır toplamlı oyun zero sum game

The situation in which the gain a participant obtains is balanced by a loss of the same magnitude belonging to the other participants.

Sıhhi Müessese

The workplace type that does not harm the environment with effects such as noise, odor and hazardous waste, by its nature. For this reason, it does not need to be located outside the settlement areas.

Sınai Mülkiyet

An intangible right ensuring that the inventions, innovations, new designs and original works in industry and agriculture are registered in the name of their first implementers, and that in the field of commerce the signs on the goods produced and sold, which will enable the distinction of their producer or seller, are registered in the name of their owners, and thereby that the first implementers have the right to produce and sell the product for a certain period.

Sınıflandırması

A classification aiming at the collection of regional statistics, their development, the making of the regions' socio-economic analyses, the determination of the framework of regional policies, and the creation of a comparable statistical database compatible with the European Union Regional Statistics System. In our country, according to this classification, 12 regions have been determined as 'Level 1', 26 sub-regions as 'Level 2', and 81 provinces as 'Level 3'.

Şeffaflık Transparency

For central banks, transparency is the provision of the information that will enable the monetary policy strategy, its aims and its implementations to be understood by the public. In this respect, transparency expresses not only the central banks' providing more information to the public, but also the being of this information understandable by the public. Transparency, a reflection of accountability, carries importance for the effectiveness of central banks' policies, because it contributes to the disclosure to the public of the monetary policy implementations and the justifications of these implementations, and thereby to the expectations forming in line with the policy targets, to the extent of credibility.

Örnek: Açıklamaların şeffaflığı yatırımcı güvenini artırdı.( Transparency of disclosures improved investor confidence.

English definition: Open and clear disclosure of relevant information.

Company Merger Merger

Companies' merging to form a larger company. While 'Merger' is a term generally used in the sense of a voluntarily carried-out merger, it can also be used for the transaction of one company's taking over another company. However, in one company's taking over another, unlike the 'merger', what is in question is an enterprise's putting an end to another enterprise's legal existence by purchasing its shares. Furthermore, in the case of a 'merger', differently from the acquisition transaction, the company formed from the merger takes a new name (generally the joint use of the two firms' names).

Example: The merger created the largest bank in the region.( The merger created the largest bank in the region.

English definition: Combination of two entities into one.

Shoe leather cost shoe leather cost

The opportunity cost of the time and effort spent with the aim of avoiding the effects of inflation.

Price floor price floor

The lowest sale price determined by the state for a good or service.

Base year base year

The year taken as the basis in calculations covering more than one year.

Bond bond

Securities with a maturity of one year or more, for which the issuing institution promises a specified repayment at maturity.

Example: The bond is measured at amortised cost.( The bond is measured at amortised cost.

English definition: A debt security paying interest.

Clearing Clearing

The transactions of the transfer of the transfer orders sent to a payment or securities settlement system, the intermediation of the mutual transmission of these orders and, in cases where pre-settlement provision is obtained, of obtaining the provision, and in some cases the netting of these orders.

Takas fiyatı clearing price

Or the market-clearing price: the price at which transactions take place when the market is in equilibrium.

Takasbank Istanbul Settlement and Custody Bank

The central clearing institution authorized to conclude the cash and securities clearing of the transactions relating to the shares, debt instruments, foreign capital market instruments, derivatives and precious metals realized in the existing markets within Borsa Istanbul. The securities delivery and receipt commitments of the Borsa Istanbul members arising from their purchase and sale transactions, and the payment commitments against the securities subject to purchase and sale, are concluded through Takasbank on an account basis. The Takasbank Electronic Transfer System (TETS) offers intermediary institutions access to the national payment system (EFT-EMKT). As the 'National Numbering Institution', Takasbank assigns ISINs (International Securities Identification Numbers), identification numbers to international standards, to the securities issued in Türkiye.

Talebin fiyat esnekliği price elasticity of demand

Or price elasticity, in short εP: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of a product decreases as a result of a one percent increase in its price.

Talebin gelir esnekliği income elasticity of demand

Or income elasticity, in short εY: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of a certain product changes as a result of a one percent increase in consumers' income.

Talebin çapraz fiyat esnekliği cross price elasticity of demand

Or cross price elasticity, in short εXP: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of one related product changes as a result of a one percent increase in another product's price.

Talep demand

A fundamental economic concept describing how much of a product the buyers in the market want to purchase, and can purchase, in a given period.

Talep eğrisi demand curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded, all else being constant.

Talep fazlası excess demand

Or a shortage: the situation in which the quantity demanded in the market exceeds the quantity supplied.

Talep yasası law of demand

A fundamental economic concept stating that, all else being constant, as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded of that good will gradually decrease or remain the same.

Talep çekişli enflasyon demand pull inflation

Inflation that arises as a result of an increase in aggregate product demand across the economy.

Talep çizelgesi demand schedule

A list showing how much of a product is demanded at different price levels in a given period.

Talep şoku demand shock

A change in aggregate demand in the economy due to an effect other than the general price level.

Tam bilgi complete information

; The situation where all relevant parties have complete information about factors that could affect an economic activity, such as price, quality, quantity, and production method.

Tam esnek ilişki perfectly elastic relationship

The other variable's responding at an infinite rate in the face of the smallest change in one variable.

Tam fiyat ayrımcılığı perfect price discrimination

Or first-degree price discrimination: the practice of selling a certain product to each buyer at the highest price that buyer is willing to pay for it.

Tam ikame perfect substitute

Products or inputs that can be used in place of one another in every case.

Tam istihdam full employment

; The unemployment rate when there is no cyclical unemployment and the actual unemployment rate equals the natural rate of unemployment.

Tam istihdam bütçe dengesi full employment budget balance

Or the structural budget balance: the public budget balance realized when the economy is at the potential GDP level.

Tam katı ilişki perfectly inelastic relationship

The other variable's not responding at all in the face of an infinite change in one variable.

Tam rekabet perfect competition

; A theoretical market structure with many buyers and sellers possessing complete information, homogeneous products, and no barriers to entry.

Tam tamamlayıcı perfect complement

Products or inputs that are used together in every case.

Tamamlayıcı mal complementary good

Products that are used together to a certain extent.

Tanıma gecikmesi recognition lag

The period passing between the formation of an adverse situation across the economy and this situation's being understood by the economists.

Tapu Senedi

The term for the official document drawn up by the Land Registry Directorate showing the owner of a real estate. Apart from real estates, a title deed can also be drawn up in the establishment of independent and perpetual rights.

Tarife tariff

The taxes the state applies to imported goods and services.

Tarihsel volatilite Historical volatility

The standard deviation calculated from the past return series; unlike implied volatility, it is based on history rather than expectations.

Tarım dışı işsizlik oranı nonfarm unemployment

The percentage showing the share of the population seeking work outside agriculture within the non-agricultural labor force in an economy.

Tarım Ürünleri Üretici Fiyat Endeksi Producer Price Index of Agriculture Products

The index measuring the price changes relating to agricultural activity within the framework of agriculture, hunting, forestry and fishing.

Tasarruf Savings

The portion of income not spent on consumption, as a result of the postponement of consumption to a future date. The desire to earn more in the future, or the instinct of taking precautions against unexpected situations that may arise later, are among the reasons increasing individuals' saving tendencies.

Tasarruf Açığı Savings Gap

In a certain period, the amount of external financing needed for investments to be able to be financed in the event that total domestic savings cannot cover total domestic investments.

Tasarruf fonksiyonu saving function

The mathematical relationship showing how private savings change, depending on fundamental variables such as the income level, in an economy.

Tavan fiyat price ceiling

The highest sale price determined by the state for a good or service.

Taşıma ticareti carry trade

Or currency carry trade: the transaction of making gains by borrowing in a currency yielding low interest and investing in a currency yielding high interest.

TCMB'nin Ağırlıklı Ortalama Faiz Oranı CBRT's Weighted Average Funding Rate

The quantity-weighted average of the CBRT's funding rates at different maturities.

Tefecilik usury

The lending of money under immoral or harassing conditions.

Tek Durak Ofis

The administrative structure ensuring that investors' bureaucratic transactions relating to their investments are concluded in the shortest time through a single authority, and employing experts within it.

Tek fiyat yasası law of one price

The view maintaining that, in the absence of transportation costs and trade barriers, product prices will be the same in every country.

Tek Hat Şeması

The diagram requested in renewable energy investments, approved by an electrical/electrical-electronics engineer, showing the electricity distribution system.
