Tekel gücü monopoly power

A buyer's or seller's being able to decide on the market price of a certain product, or to prevent competition.

Tekel ya da monopol monopoly

A market structure in which a product without close substitutes is supplied by a single seller, and obstacles lie before the entry of other sellers into the market.

Tekelci monopolist

The firm that is the sole seller of a product without close substitutes.

Tekelci rekabet monopolistic competition

; A market structure with many buyers and sellers possessing incomplete information, product differentiation, and no barriers to entry.

Tekelci sömürü monopolist exploitation

The difference arising, owing to imperfect competition, between a production factor's price and its marginal revenue product.

Teknik Analiz Technical Analysis

The making of price forecasts for the future by analyzing past-period market movements on the basis of indicators such as price and volume. For this purpose, use is made of various chart formations and statistical methods. It rests on the assumption that the formations arising on the charts because of past price movements constitute an indicator for the future, and hence that such formations can be used as an indicator for purchases and sales. Such analyses predict, for example, that the lowest prices realized in the past — in other words, the points at which prices began to rise — are 'support points', and hence these points should be awaited (be the criterion) for purchases, and again that the highest prices realized in the past are 'resistance' points and should be taken into account for sales.

Teknik Destek Programı

The support program provided by the Development Agencies, through their own personnel or, in cases of necessity, through procurement of services, to the institutional-quality and capacity-developing activities of non-profit institutions and organizations for works that can contribute to local and regional development.

Teknokent

The organized research and business center in which universities, research institutions and industrial organizations pursue their research, development and innovation activities in the same environment, produce value-added products, carry out knowledge and technology transfer among one another, and the academic, economic and social structure is integrated.

Teknoloji Geliştirme Bölgesi

The organized research and business center in which universities, research institutions and industrial organizations pursue their research, development and innovation activities in the same environment, produce value-added products, carry out knowledge and technology transfer among one another, and the academic, economic and social structure is integrated.

Teknolojik bilgi technological knowledge

The accumulation of knowledge regarding how the resources will be used in the production process.

Tektip ürün homogenous product

Products that can be offered by different sellers but that are indistinguishable, in the consumer's eyes, in form and quality.

Telif hakkı copyright

The legal privileges held for a certain period over a literary or artistic work.

Example: Copyright was recognized as an intangible non-current asset.( The copyright was recognised as an intangible asset.)

İngilizce tanım: A legal right over creative works.

Temettü dağıtım oranı Payout ratio

Shows what portion of net profit is distributed as dividends (Dividends / Net profit); the remainder is reinvested as internal funding.

Temettü verimi Dividend yield

The ratio of annual dividends per share to the share price; it shows the investor's cash return.

Example: Dividend yield was used as an input in the valuation.( The dividend yield was used as an input in the valuation.)

English definition: Annual dividend per share divided by the share price.

Teminat

The instruments, such as bank guarantee letters, Credit Guarantee Fund Inc. (KGF) suretyship letters, real estates and securities, requested by the financing institutions from the investors during their applications, and by which they secure to a certain extent the financing risk they will bear, through the speed at which they can be converted into money. Assignment: the transfer of the receivable right to someone else.

Temporarily Joint Control

Two or more undertakings' having a determining influence, for a limited period of time, over the decision-making mechanism of another undertaking.

Temsili para representative money

General payment instruments that have no significant concrete use value but that can, when desired, be converted into a certain amount of valuable metal.

Tepki fonksiyonu reaction function

The mathematical relationship describing how an economic unit's behavior changes depending on the other economic units.

Tercihlerin bütünlüğü completeness of preferences

The fundamental decision-making principle stating that the consumer can always make a choice by ranking the different product bundles.

Tercihlerin doymazlığı non-satiation of goods

The fundamental decision-making principle stating that the consumer will always prefer the larger quantity to the smaller.

transitivity of preferences transitivity of preferences

The fundamental decision-making principle stating that the consumer ranks their preferences rationally and consistently.

continuity of preferences continuity of preferences

The fundamental decision-making principle stating that there is no jump or interruption among the consumer's preferences.

reverse price discrimination reverse price discrimination

Or fourth-degree price discrimination: the practice of selling a certain product to each buyer at the same price even though its cost differs for different buyers.

Reverse Repo Reverse Repurchase Agreement

Reverse repo transactions are generally carried out, in cases of a temporary liquidity surplus in the market, with the aim of withdrawing the excess liquidity. The central bank sells the instruments in its portfolio to the institutions authorized to conduct open market operations, with a commitment to buy them back at a future date (at the price determined during the transaction). The repurchase price is likewise determined on the date the sale transaction is made. The institution party to the transaction also undertakes to sell the instrument subject to the reverse repo transaction to the central bank at the transaction's maturity. From the central bank's perspective, the reverse repo transaction expresses the temporary withdrawal of liquidity from the market, within the framework of open market operations, for the duration of the transaction's maturity, in return for the instruments given.

adverse selection adverse selection

The situation of the party with less information regarding an economic activity making a mistaken choice, with a higher probability than the other party.

Series Series

The banknotes put into circulation with changes made, outside the graphic design and dimensions of the banknotes in circulation, in their authorized signatures, motifs or colors, the printing techniques used, and the security features.

Tevsî Yatırım

The investments directed toward increasing capacity through the addition of a production line or machinery and equipment to an existing investment, and forming a whole by creating common infrastructure with the existing facility. TEYDEB: the abbreviation of the Presidency of Technology and Innovation Support Programs, which administers the incentives and supports offered by the Presidency of the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK).

Over the Counter - OTC Over the Counter - OTC

The unorganized markets not gathered under a specific structure. The transactions are carried out among the parties through mutual agreement.

Over the Counter "OTC" Derivatives Markets Over the Counter "OTC" Derivatives Markets

The market in which derivative products whose transaction conditions can be flexibly determined by the persons party to the contract are bought and sold. Since the purchase and sale transactions are not carried out on organized platforms like exchanges, it is defined in the over-the-counter market class.

commercial paper rate commercial paper rate

The interest rate of the short-term private-sector bills with a maturity of at most 270 days.

"Ticari serbestleşme" "trade liberalization"

A country's removal of the restrictions on its exports and imports, and its adopting free trade policies.

"Toplam arz" "aggregate supply"

Or in short AS: the total quantity of final goods and services that all the units in the economy want to produce and can produce in a given period.

"Toplam değişken gider" "total variable cost"

Or in short TVC: the total of all the variable costs incurred for a certain quantity of product.

"Toplam fayda" "total utility"

Or in short TU: the quantity of utility obtained from all the products consumed in a given period.

"Toplam gelir" "total revenue"

Or in short TR: the revenue obtained in return for selling a certain quantity of product at a certain price.

"Toplam gider" "total cost"

Or in short TC: the total of all the costs incurred for a certain quantity of product.

"Toplam sabit gider" "total fixed cost"

Or in short TFC: the total of all the fixed costs incurred for a certain quantity of product.

"Toplam talep" "aggregate demand"

Or in short AD: the total quantity of final goods and services that all the units in the economy want to purchase and can purchase in a given period.

"Toplam talep eğrisi" "aggregate demand curve"

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the general price level and the total production demanded, all else being constant.

"Toplam çıktı" "total output"

Or total product, in short TP: the quantity of product obtained depending on the quantity of production factors used in a given period.

Toplam ürün total product

Or total output, in short TP: the quantity of product obtained depending on the quantity of production factors used in a given period.

Toplumsal kayıp ya da dara kaybı deadweight loss

The fall in the economic surplus as a result of more or less of a product being bought and sold in the market than the level ensuring economic efficiency.

Toplumsal refah social welfare

Deciding, with limited resources, which products will be produced, how, and for whom, in a way that will benefit the whole of society.

Toprak land

Or natural resource, in short N: the fundamental production factor denoting land that can be cultivated or built upon, as well as any kind of resource coming from the land and nature.

Toprak piyasası land market

The physical or virtual environment where land and natural resources are bought and sold, and in this process the rent rate of land is determined.

Toprak piyasası dengesi land market equilibrium

The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of land demanded in the market equals the quantity of land supplied.

Toprağın kira oranı rental rate of land

Or in short PN: the payment made for using one unit of land or natural resource in production.

Toprağın marjinal ürün geliri marginal revenue product of land

Or in short MRPN: the change seen in total revenue when the quantity of land or natural resources is increased by one unit.

TOSHP Öncelikli Ürün Listesi

The list determined by the Ministry of Industry and Technology, taking into account various criteria such as foreign trade data, demand development and competition intensity, containing the products in the medium-high and high-technology sectors and the products critical for these sectors' development. TSE: the abbreviation of the Turkish Standards Institution, the institution authorized to determine the Turkish standards made compulsory or precautionary by legal regulations within Türkiye, in respect of all kinds of articles and products and of procedures and services.

Transfer ödemesi transfer payment

The legal payments made by the state without any purchase of a good or service in return.

Treynor oranı Treynor ratio

The ratio of the excess return to the systematic risk: (Rp − Rf) / βp. It is the alternative to Sharpe in well-diversified portfolios.

Mortgage Loans Mortgage

Refers to a type of real estate financing system envisaging the extension of long-term housing credits against the mortgage to be realized over real estates such as houses and plots, by a bank or a similar financial institution. In this system, individuals make a certain down payment for the real estate they request, and the remaining amount is covered by the financial institution lending it. The said financial institution has the authority to seize the real estate until the amount it has lent (the credit) is repaid. The repayment of the debt can be realized with fixed or variable interest, following a predetermined payment series. Financial institutions can issue bonds and borrow by showing the mortgage credits they have extended as collateral.

Prisoners' dilemma prisoners' dilemma

The game theory concept describing the players who cannot cooperate among themselves and act in their own interest ending up, as a result, in the situation that is not the best for them.

Thrift paradox paradox of thrift

The view maintaining that, in a closed economy, if more is saved for the purpose of thrift, income will fall, and hence savings will decrease as they try to increase them.

Consumer equilibrium consumer equilibrium

The situation in which the consumer's total utility is at its maximum, under the budget and product price constraints.

Consumer Tendency Survey Consumer Tendency Survey

A survey applied monthly with the aim of measuring consumers' current-situation assessments of their personal financial situations and of the general economy, their expectations for the coming period, and their expenditure and saving tendencies in the near future.

Consumer surplus consumer surplus

The difference between the highest price the buyer is willing to pay for a product and the product's lower price in the market.

Consumer price index consumer price index

Or in short CPI, a price index based on goods and services oriented toward the consumption of the average household as the product basket.

Example: The economy was considered hyperinflationary because the cumulative consumer price index exceeded 100 per cent over three years.( The economy was considered hyperinflationary because the cumulative consumer price index exceeded 100 per cent over three years.

English definition: A measure of the average change over time in the prices paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services.

Consumer Price Index - CPI Consumer Price Index - CPI

An index measuring changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers. In calculating the CPI, first the expenditures made over a year on goods and services by a sample population representing the country as a whole are compiled. According to this expenditure structure, the relative weights of goods and services within the index are determined; goods and services consumed in large amounts by the sample population carry higher weights, while less-consumed ones carry lower weights. The prices of the determined goods and services are collected from all provinces on specific days of each month. The CPI is calculated using the collected prices and the weights set at the start of the year.

Consumer Confidence Index - CCI Consumer Confidence Index - CCI

An indicator in which the answers given to the different questions of the Consumer Tendency Survey are evaluated together and summarized, with the aim of following the developments in consumer confidence.

consumption function consumption function

The mathematical relationship showing how private consumption expenditures change, depending on fundamental variables such as the income level, in an economy.

excludability in consumption excludability in consumption

Or in short excludability: the possibility of preventing persons who have not purchased a good or service from using that good or service.

rivalry in consumption rivalry in consumption

The inability of others to use a good or service at the same time as one person uses it.

Derivative Transactions Derivative Transactions

The transactions in which the maturity, quantity and price of an instrument (currency, interest, commodity) whose delivery will take place on a future date beyond the spot (two business days) transaction date are determined today and bound by contract. Forwards, futures, swaps and options are examples of such transactions.

derived demand derived demand

Or indirect demand: the situation where the demand for an object depends on the demand for the good, service or investment instrument produced or acquired by using that object.

Derivative Products Derivative Products

The financial instruments whose return is linked to another instrument's return — in other words, derived from another instrument's return. Futures and option contracts are examples of these instruments. Such instruments can be derived over any kind of product, such as currency, interest and gold. In such a case, for example, in an option contract written on foreign currency, the return of the option contract will depend on the movement in the market of the currency from whose return it was derived.

U

International Investment Position International Investment Position

The international investment position is the statistic showing, at a certain date, the stock value of the financial receivables of the resident persons in an economy from non-resident persons, of their financial assets in the form of gold held as reserve assets, and of the residents' financial liabilities to non-resident persons.

Undertakings

The units that are real and legal persons producing, marketing and selling goods or services in the market, that can take decisions independently, and that constitute an economic whole. (See Competition Act, Art. 3) Since the principle of economic unity is adopted in the said definition, a subsidiary is evaluated not on its own, but together with the other company or companies to which it is affiliated.

Undertakings

Refers to the decisions taken by the undertaking associations. According to Article 4 of the Competition Act, the decisions and actions of the undertaking associations carrying the aim of preventing, distorting or restricting competition directly or indirectly in a certain market for goods or services, or producing or being capable of producing this effect, are unlawful and prohibited.

Unique Transaction Reference

Number: the unique transaction reference number, expressing the combination of letters, numbers and symbols determined by the payment service provider, in conformity with the payment and settlement or messaging system protocols used for electronic transfer. UN Convention against Corruption: the UN Convention against Corruption, adopted by the UN General Assembly on 31 October 2003. The Convention contains the measures that the public and private sectors must take within the scope of preventing corruption, the anti-corruption units, and

Ur-Ge Support Program

The abbreviation of the Program for the Support of the Development of International Competitiveness, offered by the Ministry of Trade to the enterprises in similar sectors that export or are considering exporting. US-97 Code: the abbreviation of the expression 'national activity and product classification' describing the good and service the enterprises will produce, during the application for the investment incentive certificate.

Util util

The theoretical unit of measurement used in cardinal utility calculation.

adaptive expectations hypothesis adaptive expectations hypothesis

The view maintaining that economic units determine their forecasts for the future on the basis of backward-looking information.

implementation lag implementation lag

The period passing between the understanding of an adverse situation formed in the economy and the taking of the measures that will correct this situation.

Applications good laboratuary practice (GLP) iyi laboratuvar

The incentive implementation in which, in the event of investment in the sectors and under the conditions determined for the provinces located in 6 different regions according to their socio-economic development levels, the support elements of VAT Exemption, Customs Duty Exemption, Tax Reduction, Insurance Premium Employer's Share Support, Interest or Profit Share Support, Income Tax Withholding Support, Insurance Premium Support and Investment Site Allocation are offered.

Long run long run

In the microeconomic context, the conceptual time interval in which entry into or exit from the market is possible and all the production factors are variable. In the macroeconomic context, it is the conceptual time interval in which prices and wages are variable and the production factors can show full mobility among regions and sectors.

long run average cost long run average cost

Or in short LRAC: the total cost incurred per unit of product in the long run, depending on the scale selected.

long run Phillips curve long run Phillips curve

Or in short LRPC: a graphical tool showing the relationship between the unemployment and inflation rates in the case where expected and realized inflation equal one another.

long run market supply curve long run market supply curve

A graphical tool showing the long-run relationship between the price of a good and the quantity supplied in the market, all else being constant.

long run aggregate supply curve long run aggregate supply curve

Or in short LRAS: a graphical tool showing the long-run relationship between the general price level and the quantity of aggregate supply, all else being constant.

Ü

Wage wage

; payments made to workers on an hourly, daily, or piece-rate basis for a specific job

wage-price spiral wage-price spiral

The self-repeating process in which the increase in wages raises the production costs, thereby reducing aggregate supply, and as a result the general price level rises and raises the wages again.

Country Risk Country Risk

Refers to the probability of loss to which any bank or institution holding, in its portfolio, the direct and/or indirect risk of the debtors in a foreign country is exposed, as a result of the debtors in that country (central government, corporate or other) failing to fulfill, or avoiding, their external obligations owing to the events and uncertainties affecting the economic, social and political conditions. Besides the deteriorated economic, political and social conditions increasing the probability of default in a country; events such as expropriation, moratorium, repudiation of debt, devaluation, and the lack of transparency in the practices of the country's supervisory authority also fall within the scope of country risk. Country risk fundamentally covers sovereign risk, transfer risk and contagion risk, and also includes the categories of indirect exchange rate risk, macroeconomic risk and indirect country risk.

producer equilibrium producer equilibrium

The situation in which total cost is at its lowest, under the total product and factor price constraints.

producer surplus producer surplus

The difference between the lowest price the seller would accept for a product and the product's higher price in the market.

producer price index producer price index

Or in short PPI: the price index taking as its product basket the goods and services produced domestically, based on the prices at which they are first offered for sale by their producers.

producer)

The name given to the manufacturing firms that produce parts, equipment or another product for another firm.

production production

The process of the conversion of the various production factors into goods and services.

Production Flow Chart

The diagram requested during the application for the investment incentive certificate, in which the investor shows the stages of production of its goods and services, also stating the number of personnel to be employed at each stage. Product Diversification: the type of investment expressing that an investment incentive certificate has been obtained with the aim of increasing the number of varieties of the product produced. Maturity: the period granted for the performance of a work for which a sanction is generally foreseen in the event of non-performance, or for the payment of a debt.

factor of production factor of production

The general name of the resources such as labor, capital and land used as inputs in production.

production function production function

The mathematical relationship showing how the quantity of product changes depending on the inputs used in the production process.

production theory production theory

The body of principles explaining what inputs a producer wishing to make profit can produce with, how much it can produce, and at what price it can sell them.

production cost production cost

The total of all the expenses incurred in the production process, chiefly the input costs, such as research and development expenditures and taxes.

production possibility frontier production possibility frontier

A graphical tool showing the various combinations of goods and services that could be produced if all the resources at hand were used in the best way.

subsidies on production subsidies on production

The payments or tax reductions the state gives in return for producing, without regard to quantity or value.

taxes on production taxes on production

The taxes paid to the state independently of the quantity or value of the good or service produced.

productive efficiency productive efficiency

The production of goods and services at the lowest possible unit cost.

product differentiation product differentiation

The development of products in ways that create a perception of difference in the consumer's eye, with the aim of gaining market power.

product market product market

Or the output market: the markets where the goods and services directed toward final consumption are bought and sold.

basket of goods basket of goods

Or the market basket of goods: the list of products determined with the aim of representing the whole of the economy or a certain subsection of it.

third degree price discrimination third degree price discrimination

The practice of selling a certain product to different buyer groups at different prices.

Third Market Tertiary Markets

The transactions made in the over-the-counter (OTC) markets are called third-market transactions.

V

Vade maturity

The repayment period or date of the debt taken.

Örnek: Tahvilin vadesi, ihraçtan itibaren on yıldır. ( The bond's maturity is ten years from issue.)

English definition: The date an instrument becomes due for settlement.

Vadeli işlem Futures contract

A standardized exchange-traded contract containing the obligation to buy or sell a specific asset at a specific price on a specific date; daily settlement (mark-to-market) applies.

Example: A futures contract is traded on an organized exchange.( The futures contract traded on an organised exchange.)

English definition: A standardised contract to buy or sell at a future date.

Vadeli İşlemler Sözleşmesi Forward Contract

It means forward transactions. It envisages the delivery of a certain instrument, at a previously determined price, again on a previously determined date. The transactions are generally not carried out in organized markets, but with the buyer and seller coming face to face, in line with the parties' needs. Such contracts, which can be arranged over instruments subject to purchase and sale such as foreign currency, securities and commodities, can be directed toward speculative aims as well as eliminating price risk.

Örnek: Vadeli işlem sözleşmesi, döviz kurunu sabitler. ( The forward contract fixes the exchange rate.)

İngilizce tanım: A contract to buy or sell at a future date.

Vadeli mevduat time deposit

Bank accounts that provide a monetary return in exchange for not using the money for a predetermined period.

Vadeli Piyasalar Futures Market

Forward markets are markets in which contracts are bought and sold that contain the commitment to deliver a specific product at a future date, on the condition that its price is fixed today.

Vadesiz mevduat demand deposit

The bank accounts into which money can be deposited and withdrawn whenever desired, or which can be used for payment purposes.

Example: A demand deposit is classified as a current liability because it can be repaid on demand.( Demand deposits are classified as current liabilities because they are repayable on call.

English definition: Deposits that the depositor may withdraw at any time without prior notice.

Vadeye Dayalı Zorunlu Karşılıklar Maturity Based Reserve Requirement

The required reserve amount that banks and other financial institutions must hold at the CBRT against their liabilities varies according to the maturity of those liabilities. Reserve requirement ratios are higher for short-term liabilities and lower for long-term ones. Thereby, by encouraging longer-term liabilities, the aim is to extend the average maturity of banks' liabilities.

Vadeye Kadar Getiri Yield to Maturity

Refers to the return that will be obtained as a result of a security being held until its maturity. Its English equivalent is also called the 'effective rate of return'.

Valör Value Date

The date on which a transaction on which agreement has been reached will actually be carried out — for example, on which receivables and debts will be mutually recorded into the accounts. Similarly, it expresses the date on which a fund, for example a deposit, can actually be used by its owner.

Varlık / Yükümlülük İlkesi Asset / Liability Principle

The asset/liability principle is based on the showing of all debts and receivables to non-residents as gross assets and liabilities for the stocks, and by netting each category for the flows.

Varlık devir hızı Asset turnover

The ratio of sales to total assets (Sales / Total Assets); it measures the effectiveness of the assets in generating sales. This is the Turkish standard, in place of 'activity coefficient'.

Varlık kârlılığı Return on Assets - ROA

The ratio of net profit to total assets (Net profit / Total Assets); it shows how efficiently the asset base generates profit.

Varlıklar assets

The balance sheet section showing the economic values held by or receivable to an organization.

Varlığa Dayalı Menkul Kıymet Asset Backed Security

The instruments of value that institutions can issue in return for the receivables that have arisen from their own commercial transactions. Consumer credits, housing credits and the receivables arising from export transactions are among the types of receivables that can be subject to this transaction. By selling asset-backed securities, banks can convert their receivables into cash beforehand.

Veblen malı Veblen good

A conspicuous-consumption good whose quantity demanded increases rather than decreases as its price rises.

Vega Vega

The sensitivity of the option price to a one percent change in volatility; an increase in volatility raises the value of call and put options.

Vergi tax

The payments that the state legally and obligatorily collects from persons and institutions with the aim of covering public expenditures.

Example: Current tax is measured at the amount expected to be paid to the tax authorities.( Current tax is measured at the amount expected to be paid to the tax authorities.

English definition: A compulsory charge levied by a government on income, profits or transactions.

Vergi İndirimi Desteği

An investor making an investment within the scope of an investment incentive certificate containing the tax reduction support element can pay income or corporate tax at reduced rates, varying according to the region where the investment is being made, and can continue benefiting from this reduction until reaching the investment contribution amount, at rates again varying by region.

Vergi Matrahı

The value or quantity taken as the basis in the calculation of the tax. The tax debt is calculated by applying a tax schedule to the base. Tax bases are of two kinds, value-based and quantity-based. An ad valorem base (value-based) is calculated taking the values of the economic elements as the basis, and a certain tax rate is set for this base. A specific base (quantity-based) is a base applied to tax subjects with low monetary value.

Vergi Muafiyeti

The transaction of the exclusion from tax, by the same or different tax laws, of the persons or groups of persons who are originally obliged to pay tax according to the tax laws.

Vergi yansıması tax incidence

The concept describing how the tax is shared between the buyers and sellers in the market.

Vergi çarpanı tax multiplier

The coefficient showing how much effect a unit change in autonomous taxes will have on equilibrium income.

Veri Depolama Kuruluşu Trade Repository

The institutions defined within the scope of the over-the-counter derivative market reform, to which the purchase and sale transaction data realized in the over-the-counter derivative markets are reported.

Y

Yakalama etkisi catch-up effect

The hypothesis that per capita income in poor countries tends to rise faster than in rich countries.

near monopsony near monopsony

A market structure in which a product supplied by more than one seller is demanded to a very large extent by a single buyer, and obstacles lie before the entry of other buyers into the market.

near monopoly near monopoly

A market structure in which a product without close substitutes is supplied to a very large extent by a single seller, and obstacles lie before entry into the market.

neutral good neutral good

; a good that is not dependent on income in market analysis and, in benefit analysis, does not provide benefits or harms to economic units.

Yapı Kullanma İzin Belgesi

( İskan Belgesi) A document issued by the licensing authority that indicates that a completed construction is fully or partially usable and that the constructed building was built as specified in the project.

Yapısal Bankacılık Reformları Structural Banking Reforms

The reforms that came to the agenda with the emergence, along with the crisis, of the problems caused by the universal banking model offering many different products and services under the same roof, and that fundamentally envisage the gathering of the departments of banks conducting their risky and complex transactions under separate legal personalities.

Yapısal Bütçe Dengesi Structural Budget Balance

The budget balance that would form in the case where the realized production level equals the potential production level; it is obtained by subtracting the cyclical budget balance from the realized budget balance. The structural budget balance is calculated with a three-stage method: in the first stage, the budget expenditures and revenues sensitive to cyclical movements must be determined, and the revenue and expenditure elasticities calculated. Secondly, potential output and output gap series are created in order to define the cyclical movements. In the third stage, the revenue and expenditure elements stemming from the cyclical movements are subtracted from the realized budget balance. In calculating the structural budget balance, the sifting out of the one-off revenue and expenditure items also carries importance.

Yapısal işsizlik structural unemployment

The type of unemployment stemming from the mismatch, in the labor market, between the skills employers seek and the skills the job seekers possess.

Yapışkan fiyatlar sticky prices

The concept describing the situation in which some prices cannot immediately respond to the supply and demand changes in the economy.

Yapışkan ücretler sticky wages

The concept describing the situation in which some wages cannot immediately respond to the supply and demand changes in the economy.

Horizontal merger horizontal merger

The merger of two rival firms located in the same market.

Investment

The investments made in the medium-low technology group, such as the manufacturing of coke and refined petroleum products, plastic products, glass and metal structural materials, determined according to the OECD technology intensity definition.

Example: The company made a long-term investment in a subsidiary.( The company made a long-term investment in a subsidiary.)

English definition: An asset held to increase wealth through income or appreciation.

Investment Survey - YA Investment Survey - IS

A survey applied twice a year with the aim of capturing the current investment tendencies of the workplaces operating in the industrial sector and their investment plans for the near future, and the assessments relating to the purpose of these investments and the factors effective in the workplace managers' investment decisions. To access the Investment Survey

Investment Advisory

In the broadest expression, the giving of written or oral opinions and advice in the works to be carried out for the investors on any investment instrument. Through investment consultancy, the investor receives consultancy services from the expert/authorized/designated institutions and organizations for the information, orientation, opinion-taking and planning activities it needs at every stage of the investment it has planned.

Investment curve investment curve

A graphical tool showing the relationship between the interest rate and planned investment expenditures, all else being constant.

Mutual Funds Mutual Funds

The form taken by the moneys collected from the public in return for participation certificates being converted, by the investment companies, into a portfolio consisting of capital market instruments and of the gold and other precious metals traded on the national and international exchanges. These funds, managed by the investment companies, provide returns to investors in different ways depending on their properties and investment areas.

investment spending multiplier investment spending multiplier

The coefficient showing how much effect a unit change in investment expenditures will have on equilibrium income.

Investment Credit

The credit obtained from external sources with the aim of meeting firms' investment needs and supporting the projects they design to develop within this scope.

Investment Partnership

The capital market institutions established in the form of joint-stock companies, on the registered capital principle, in order to operate a portfolio of capital market instruments and of gold and other precious metals traded on the national and international exchanges or on the off-exchange organized markets.

Example: An investment partnership provides its members with membership rights.( A mutual entity provides its members with membership rights.

English definition: An entity whose owners receive dividends or returns rather than equity shares.

Investment Incentive System

The program brought into force with the 'Decree Amending the Decree on State Aids in Investments No. 2012/3305', offering incentive facilities directed toward investors.

Investment Site Allocation

The allocation of public land, with the Investment Incentive Certificate, to the sectoral investments supported within the scope of the 'Decree Amending the Decree on State Aids in Investments No. 2012/3305'. Investment Contribution Ratio: the ratio found by dividing the investment contribution amount by the total investment made.

Investment Contribution Amount

The portion of the investments to be covered by the State through the tax forgone from collection, by applying the reduced corporate tax.

Investor

The person who puts capital into various investment instruments in order to make profit, gain advantage, increase capital accumulation, or obtain income in various periods.

Example: The investor assessed whether it had significant influence over the associate.( The investor assessed whether it had significant influence over the associate.

English definition: A party that holds an interest in another entity, such as through shares, and is entitled to returns from that investment.

Investment Exit

An entrepreneur's or investor's transferring the venture after reaching an investment or return of the dimensions they wish.

Investment

The livestock investments including, alongside breeding, the investments of dairy products production, meat products production, slaughterhouse, cold storage warehouse and feed unit.

Economic Analysis of the Investment

The method of examining, from the standpoint of the country's economy, the cost-benefit analysis prepared for the investment. The economic analysis of the investment is comprehensive in scope and includes the whole of society in the examination.

Payback Period of the Investment

The total period over which the investment amount is recovered with the income or value increase obtained after the investment made in any investment instrument.

Internal Rate of Return of the Investment

The discount rate that equalizes the net present value of an investment project to zero — in other words, that equalizes the present value of the cash inflows to the present value of the cash outflows.

Technical Analysis of the Investment

The method of being able to predict, for any investment instrument carried out, the price movements that may form in the future, by looking at past price movements.

arc elasticity arc elasticity

The elasticity calculation method used to find the average elasticity between two points on a curve or line.

new Keynesian economic theory new Keynesian economic theory

The school of thought aiming to ground Keynesian economic theory on microeconomic foundations, and advocating the state's intervention in the economy through monetary and fiscal policy.

new classical economic theory new classical economic theory

The school of thought maintaining that the changes seen in real income in the short run stem from unpredictable demand shocks, and advocating that the state should not intervene in the economy.

Restructuring Restructuring

All the activities of a financial market infrastructure institution — including the replenishment of the financial resources previously established but exhausted, and various liquidity arrangements — with the aim of resolving any unmet loss, liquidity shortage or capital insufficiency problem that has arisen because of participant default or other reasons (business, operational or other structural weaknesses), and that has remained unresolved despite the use of the normal mechanisms, in conformity with the relevant legislation it is subject to, its own internal rules and procedures, and its contractual obligations.

Örnek: Yeniden yapılandırma iki üretim tesisini kapattı. ( The restructuring closed two production plants.)

English definition: Programme that materially changes the scope or manner of operations.

Yenilenebilir Enerji

Energy obtained from the energy flows present in continuously ongoing natural processes. Renewable energy sources can be listed as solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, hydraulic energy, biomass energy and hydrogen energy.

Yerel Yönetim Bütçesi Local Government Budget

; It is the budget of organizations such as municipalities and special provincial administrations within the local government scope.

Yetmiş kuralı rule of seventy

The rule of thumb for approximately finding, as 70 / growth rate, the number of periods needed for a variable to double.

Yeşil alan yatırımı green-field investment

The type of foreign direct investment containing the physical investments that foreigners establish or build from scratch domestically.

Yeşil GSYH Green GDP

The national income calculation proposed in 2006 by the People's Republic of China, taking into account also the effects of economic production on the environment.

Yoksulluk sınırı poverty line

The lowest income needed for an average household in a country to be able to meet its fundamental needs.

Yola Terk

The transaction of the landowners, during the realization of the development plans, relinquishing the whole or a part of the real estate, with or without consideration, in conformity with the development plan, to the public benefit (road, green space, park, etc.). Contractor: the person who undertakes to carry out a work relating to construction and trade for someone else.

Yoğunlaşma oranı concentration ratio

Or in short CR: the market concentration measure calculated by summing the market shares of the largest certain number of firms in a market.

Yurt Dışı Üretici Fiyat Endeksi - YD-ÜFE Non-Domestic Producer Price Index - NDPPI

The index measuring the price changes in the consumption, intermediate and capital goods produced for export abroad, and in the energy sector.

Domestic Demand Domestic Demand

The total of final domestic demand and the stock change.

Domestic Producer Price Index (YI-UFE) Domestic Producer Price Index - D-PPI

The index measuring the price changes in the consumption, intermediate and capital goods produced for domestic trade, and in the energy sector.

Managed Floating Exchange Rate Regime Managed Floating Exchange Rate Regime

The exchange rate regime in which the exchange rates are freely determined in the market without an official exchange rate target, but the authorities can intervene in the rates by selling foreign currency to the market or buying foreign currency from the market.

managed floating exchange rate managed floating exchange rate

The exchange rate regime in which the nominal exchange rates are determined by the market, but the monetary authority intervenes in the rate as it deems necessary.

Directional Principle Directional Principle

The principle of investment by direction rests on the determination of the direction of direct investment — in other words, whether the investment is made domestically or abroad.

predatory pricing predatory pricing

The practice of lowering the price excessively for a temporary period, with the aim of destroying competition.

Annualization Annualization

The conversion of short-period returns or volatility to the annual scale; return scales as (1+r)^t−1 and volatility as σ√t (the square-root rule).

time-related underemployment time-related underemployment

The persons who are in employment, work less than a weekly total of 40 hours, but want to work longer and could start working more if they found work.

Loss aversion Loss aversion

According to Kahneman-Tversky's Prospect Theory, the feeling of losses approximately twice as heavily as equivalent gains; one of its consequences is the investor's being late to sell the losing position.

Zero-Price Economy / Markets

The zero-price economy is the business model, seen particularly in multi-sided markets, based on goods or services offered to the consumer or user having no price whatsoever, but being offered in return for the consumer or user incurring a cost other than money (for example the provision of their personal data or being exposed to advertisements).

Zeyilname

ABİGEM: the European Union Türkiye Business Development Centers (ABİGEM), the organizations offering SMEs training and consultancy services in the areas they need, operating with the status of joint-stock companies established under the leadership of TOBB in the partnership of the relevant Chambers of Commerce and/or Industry.

Zihinsel muhasebe Mental accounting

The setting aside of money into mental pockets according to its source and purpose of use; it conflicts with the principle of the fungibility of money.

Zincirleme hacim endeksi chain linked volume index

A series of numbers measuring the real income estimates of different periods using the average prices of the previous period.

Zirve peak

The point at which economic activity reaches its highest level at the end of an expansion process.

Zorunlu Karşılık Oranı Reserve Requirement Ratio

The statutory ratio showing the amount of reserves that banks and other financial institutions are required to hold at the central bank against the deposits, loans and similar liabilities on their balance sheets. The reserve requirement ratio may differ according to the type, maturity and currency of the liabilities. Central banks can use this ratio as a monetary policy instrument. If banks do not hold idle reserves, an increase in the reserve requirement ratio leads banks to call back the loans they have extended, which causes the money supply to contract. When the ratio is lowered, part of the required reserves turns into usable reserves, which increases the banks' lending base; the expansion of the banks' lending base in turn causes the money supply to grow.

Zorunlu mal necessity good

Products whose demand in the market does not change, or increases at a lower rate, when the average income level rises.

Zorunlu rezerv required reserve

The money a bank is obliged to hold in its account at the central bank, depending on the amount of deposits it has collected.

Zımni volatilite Implied volatility

The volatility backed out from the option's market price; it is the market's measurable expectation of future volatility.

X

X-Inefficiency

'X-inefficiency', first put forward by Leibenstein in 1956, is the increase in welfare loss as a result of the monopolistic firm's not reducing its costs to the lowest possible level (paying high salaries, excessive employment, etc.), because it feels no competitive pressure whatsoever.
